We derive a general sufficient condition for such an interior optimum and show that finite-time Ornstein-Uhlenbeck correlations satisfy the required fast-switching asymptotics, whereas the white-noise limit need not. Finite-size simulations reproduce the nonmonotonic threshold, its shift toward slower switching as [MATH] increases, antiphase composite order in a nonmagnetic state, and mode mixing on a magnetized background.
tldr: A classical stochastic Ising-Kuramoto model shows a nonmonotonic synchronization threshold optimized by a finite spin switching rate due to memory from Ornstein-Uhlenbeck phase noise.
motivation: The paper studies how memory in phase dynamics affects the competition between spin relaxation and phase coherence in a globally coupled system.
method: Linear response analysis around the nonmagnetic incoherent state yields the synchronization threshold as a memory-weighted Laplace transform of the free phase correlation function; finite-size simulations support the results.
result: An interior optimal switching rate minimizes the threshold, and finite-time Ornstein-Uhlenbeck correlations satisfy the required fast-switching asymptotics, unlike the white-noise limit; simulations reproduce nonmonotonic threshold, antiphase composite order, and mode mixing.
conclusion: Memory-induced optimal switching is a generic feature of this dynamic Ising-Kuramoto model and demonstrates the importance of finite correlation times for synchronization thresholds.

title: Coherent Energy Cascades In Nonlinear Disordered Hamiltonians
authors: Anxo Biasi, Brad Cownden, Oleg Evnin, Alvaro Iturbe Jabaloyes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The familiar wave kinetic theory revolves around turbulent energy cascades characterized by random phases of the individual normal modes. By contrast, recent years have revealed turbulent cascades where the transfer of energy is mediated by phase-coherent dynamics. Such coherent cascades have been previously established in deterministic systems with a tightly controlled algebraic structure of the mode interactions, such as nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations. Here, we show that the presence of phase-coherent cascades is robust with respect to substantial alterations of the mode couplings. We prove that, in infinite-dimensional resonant Hamiltonian systems with fully resonant normal mode spectra and random nonlinear couplings, a structured subset of couplings --- an infinitesimal fraction of the total --- suffices to support coherent cascades characterized by phase alignment, the formation of power-law spectra, and either unbounded growth of Sobolev norms or a finite-time blow-up. Numerical simulations further demonstrate the emergence of coherent cascades from random initial data through a process of phase locking, suggesting a mechanism for their emergence in broader classes of initial data and systems. We thus show that disordered mode interactions can sustain, rather than block, coherent energy transport across arbitrarily distant scales.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that coherent energy cascades, previously known in deterministic nonlinear Schrödinger systems, persist even with random nonlinear couplings in infinite-dimensional resonant Hamiltonian systems.
motivation: Wave turbulence typically involves random-phase cascades, but recent work found phase-coherent cascades in algebraically structured systems; it was unclear whether these survive substantial alterations of mode couplings.
method: The authors prove the existence of coherent cascades in infinite-dimensional resonant Hamiltonian systems with fully resonant spectra and random nonlinear couplings, supported by a structured subset of couplings, and perform numerical simulations showing phase locking.
result: They show power-law spectra, phase alignment, and either unbounded Sobolev norm growth or finite-time blow-up from an infinitesimal fraction of couplings; numerics reveal emergence from random initial data through phase locking.
conclusion: Disordered mode interactions can sustain rather than block coherent energy transport across arbitrarily distant scales, broadening the scope of coherent cascades in nonlinear wave systems.

title: Independent Density And Coherence Skin Effects In Adaptive Fermion Circuits
authors: Karim Chahine, Markus Siegl, Michael Buchhold
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive circuits use measurements and outcome-conditioned feedback to implement nonreciprocal dynamics without postselection. We show that fermion circuits host independently tunable density and coherence skin effects. The stationary state has an exact density tilt set only by measurement strength and feedback displacement: conditioned-gate details cancel, yielding an exponential one-particle profile and, at any filling, a tilted ensemble of configuration weights. Decaying coherences instead obey, in the bulk, an effective Hatano-Nelson generator controlled by the conditioned gates through a relative occupation phase. Tuning this phase drives a point-gap topological transition and reverses coherence localization at fixed density, allowing density and coherence to localize at opposite edges. We derive both exponents for conditioned [MATH] gates and propose a correlator-ratio probe using ensemble-averaged observables.
tldr: Adaptive fermion circuits with measurements and feedback exhibit independently tunable density and coherence skin effects, where the density tilt depends only on measurement strength and feedback displacement while coherence localization is controlled by conditioned gates.
motivation: To implement nonreciprocal dynamics without postselection using adaptive circuits, and to study non-Hermitian skin effects in fermionic systems.
method: The authors analyze adaptive fermion circuits with conditioned gates, derive the stationary-state density tilt and an effective Hatano-Nelson generator for decaying coherences, and propose a correlator-ratio probe using ensemble-averaged observables.
result: The density tilt is set solely by measurement strength and feedback displacement, while coherence localization is governed by a relative occupation phase; tuning this phase drives a point-gap topological transition and can localize density and coherence at opposite edges.
conclusion: Adaptive fermion circuits offer a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics without postselection, with potential applications in quantum simulation and topological quantum computing.

title: From Projected Subspaces To Full-Space Implementations: Representation-Equivalence Audits For Open-Shell Adapt-vqe
authors: Petr Klenovsk\'y Lucia Mal\'i\v{c}kov\'a
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A variational state optimized in a symmetry-projected space need not be the state prepared by exponentiating the corresponding unprojected parent generators. For an orthogonal target-space projector [MATH], [MATH], and an anti-Hermitian generator [MATH], exact equivalence for all amplitudes requires target-space invariance, [MATH]. We formulate this condition as a representation-equivalence audit for open-shell ADAPT-VQE. For a canonical CAS(15e,9o) type-1 Cu(II) Hamiltonian, 274 of 323 bare Hartree--Fock-origin single, double, and triple excitations violate this condition. Projected-doublet ADAPT reaches 1.5719 m[MATH] with 121 operators, whereas the same amplitudes in the corresponding full-space sequence give 464.730 m[MATH] error, 0.07343 fidelity with the projected state, and 54.45\% quartet weight. Reoptimizing the same 121 parent generators in the same order under the hard constraint [MATH] reduces the best converged error to 8.482 m[MATH], showing that the catastrophic same-angle failure is primarily a representation/parameter-transfer failure but is not completely repaired by full-space reoptimization of the fixed sequence. An independent 12-qubit NO benchmark exhibits the same mechanism more mildly. A spin-preserving generalized full-space construction removes the representation ambiguity and reaches 1.493 and 1.181 m[MATH] at 18 and 24 qubits. For the 18-qubit positive control, selectively refining only four Suzuki-2 factors and re-transpiling with a fixed compiler seed passes the predeclared circuit-equivalence gate at 19,660 controlled-X (CX) gates and depth 23,016. Circuit synthesis and final-energy measurement therefore constitute separate validation layers. The contribution is a validation framework, not a new spin-adapted ADAPT algorithm.
tldr: The paper introduces a representation-equivalence audit for open-shell ADAPT-VQE, showing that projected-space optimized amplitudes can fail catastrophically when transferred to full-space implementations.
motivation: Variational states optimized in a symmetry-projected subspace may not be preparable by exponentiating the corresponding unprojected parent generators, creating a hidden validation gap in quantum chemistry circuits.
method: The authors derive a target-space invariance condition for exact equivalence and audit a CAS(15e,9o) Cu(II) Hamiltonian, comparing projected-doublet ADAPT-VQE against full-space same-angle and reoptimized sequences, with an independent 12-qubit NO benchmark and circuit synthesis checks.
result: For the Cu(II) case, 274 of 323 bare excitations violate the equivalence condition; same-angle full-space execution gives 464.730 mHa error and 0.073 fidelity, while full-space reoptimization only reduces error to 8.482 mHa, and a spin-preserving generalized construction reaches 1.493 and 1.181 mHa at 18 and 24 qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a validation framework rather than a new spin-adapted ADAPT algorithm, highlighting that circuit synthesis and final-energy measurement are separate validation layers for projected-to-full-space implementations.

title: Transverse Momentum As The Counter-diabatic Generator In Bent Waveguide Couplers
authors: Shuo-Yen Tseng Yu-Kai Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bending the axis of a mode-evolution coupler suppresses the nonadiabatic coupling between its supermodes, and bent couplers of this kind were recently shown to realize the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol. Here we identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement of a waveguide structure is generated by the transverse momentum [MATH], whose diagonal matrix elements vanish in a real supermode basis and whose off-diagonal element is purely imaginary; in a two-mode system such an operator is proportional to [MATH]. The CD term of a two-waveguide coupler is itself proportional to [MATH], while the detuning and the coupling, the two parameters set by the waveguide widths and spacing, lie in the [MATH]--[MATH] plane and cannot produce it. The transverse momentum is therefore the CD generator of the bent coupler, by necessity rather than by design. Equating the term it supplies to the nonadiabatic coupling gives the axis slope in closed form as a ratio of two matrix elements of the unperturbed supermodes at a single cross section, which a commutator identity recasts in coupled-mode variables as [MATH]. The expression agrees with the numerical offset search to [MATH] and requires no search. Beam propagation simulations confirm the design and compare it, for the first time, with the CD protocol realized by unitary transformation in a straight coupler built from the same reference structure. The two devices reach [MATH] and [MATH] supermode fidelity where the untreated coupler reaches [MATH], and agree in bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, while their internal trajectories differ by exactly the frame transformation that relates them.
tldr: The paper identifies transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers and derives a closed-form expression for the axis slope, validated by beam propagation simulations.
motivation: Counter-diabatic protocols enable fast adiabatic-like mode evolution, but the underlying generator in bent waveguide couplers was previously unidentified.
method: The authors analyze a two-mode waveguide coupler, show that the transverse momentum operator has the required purely imaginary off-diagonal element proportional to the CD term, and derive the axis slope via a commutator identity, comparing with numerical offset search and beam propagation simulations.
result: The closed-form slope agrees with numerical search to high precision, and the bent coupler achieves improved supermode fidelity versus an untreated coupler, matching bandwidth and fabrication tolerance of a straight CD coupler.
conclusion: Transverse momentum is necessarily the CD generator of the bent coupler, providing a design principle for compact, robust mode-evolution devices.

title: Acoustoelectrically Enhanced Acousto-optic Modulation In An Integrated Silicon Nitride And Thin Film Lithium Niobate Platform
authors: Matthew J. Storey, John H. Dallyn, Kiyan Hocek, Michael Miller, Peter T. Rakich, Scott A. Diddams, Nils T. Otterstrom, Matt Eichenfield
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acoustoelectric interactions in piezoelectric-semiconductor heterostructures allow the propagation characteristics of microwave frequency phonons in piezoelectric media to be controlled and radically enhanced, providing electrically controllable phonon gain, large velocity tuning, isolation, and circulation, as well as extremely large electron-mediated phononic nonlinearities. Here, for the first time, we create such a piezoelectric-semiconductor heterostructure with lithium-niobate-on-insulator and InGaAs that also supports guided optical modes through the addition of a silicon nitride waveguide and modification of the acoustic materials to provide an optical lower cladding. We use this new architecture to demonstrate acoustoelectrically enhanced acousto-optic modulation, where 1 GHz phonons are piezoelectrically generated and acoustoelectrically amplified on-chip by up to 60 dB before impinging on the optical waveguide, providing pure phase modulation with a [MATH] figure-of-merit of 0.077 V-cm while only consuming 3.77 mW of DC electrical power to provide the amplification. We then consider future applications enabled by these functionalities and describe a novel tunable optical delay and an optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) analog---an acoustoelectrically enhanced opto-acoustic oscillator (AE-OAO). We show that using Brillouin optomechanical transduction and acoustoelectrically lossless acoustic time delay, the AE-OAO could replace kilometers of optical fiber delay used in OEOs but on a single, centimeter-scale chip.
tldr: The paper demonstrates an integrated acoustoelectric acousto-optic modulator using a lithium-niobate-on-insulator and InGaAs heterostructure with a silicon nitride waveguide, achieving 60 dB on-chip phonon amplification and pure phase modulation.
motivation: Acoustoelectric interactions in piezoelectric-semiconductor heterostructures can control and enhance microwave phonon propagation, enabling functionalities like phonon gain and velocity tuning. The authors aim to integrate such interactions with guided optical modes for enhanced acousto-optic modulation on chip.
method: They fabricate a piezoelectric-semiconductor platform combining lithium niobate on insulator with InGaAs and add a silicon nitride optical waveguide. 1 GHz phonons are piezoelectrically generated and acoustoelectrically amplified before interacting with the optical waveguide.
result: The device achieves up to 60 dB acoustoelectric amplification and pure phase modulation with a figure-of-merit of 0.077 V-cm while consuming only 3.77 mW of DC power. They also propose an acoustoelectrically enhanced opto-acoustic oscillator for replacing fiber delay lines.
conclusion: This platform enables compact, low-power acousto-optic modulation and tunable optical delay, with potential applications in optoelectronic oscillators and integrated photonics.

title: Localization Transition In Kinetically Deformed One-dimensional Aubry-Andr\'e Model
authors: Arpita Goswami
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a [MATH]-deformation in the single-particle kinetic energy and investigate how it modifies the localization in the one-dimensional Aubry-Andr\'e (AA) model. We construct a Hermitian [MATH]-deformed kinetic operator as a nonlinear function of the lattice translation operator, preserving the uniform lattice and recovering the conventional AA Hamiltonian continuously in the undeformed limit [MATH]. The deformation generates an infinite set of correlated odd-range kinetic processes, controlled by a single parameter q, rather than phenomenologically involving long-range hopping. Under the dual transformation, this long-range hopping appears as higher harmonics of the dual quasiperiodic potential, providing a controlled route for breaking the exact self-duality of the AA model, with [MATH] as the control parameter, consequently modifying the localization structure for [MATH]. In contrast to the conventional AA model, where all eigenstates localize simultaneously at [MATH], the deformed model exhibits a fraction of delocalized states even beyond [MATH]. An intermediate regime also emerges in the [MATH] plane where localized and extended eigenstates coexist across the spectrum. We also propose a possible experimental realization of the hierarchy produced in the [MATH]-deformed kinetic setting in a periodically driven AA model.
tldr: The paper introduces a q-deformation of the kinetic energy in the 1D Aubry-André model, showing that it breaks self-duality and leads to modified localization transitions including coexisting localized and extended states.
motivation: To investigate how a nonlinear kinetic deformation alters the localization structure of a canonical quasiperiodic model beyond the standard Aubry-André transition.
method: A Hermitian q-deformed kinetic operator is constructed as a nonlinear function of the lattice translation operator, generating correlated odd-range hopping; the dual transformation and spectrum are analyzed, with a proposed experimental realization in a periodically driven AA model.
result: The deformation yields an intermediate regime in the parameter plane where localized and extended eigenstates coexist, and a fraction of delocalized states persists beyond the conventional transition point.
conclusion: The q-deformed Aubry-André model provides a tunable platform for engineering localization transitions and suggests a route to experimental observation via periodically driven systems.

title: The "Gate Of Fate" - A Quantum Gaming Concept
authors: Deeptanshu Malu, Deevyanshu Malu, Bhaskaran Muralidharan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum physics underpins the emerging quantum technology era, yet its counterintuitive principles remain challenging for beginners. Video games offer a promising medium to make these principles accessible through an interactive experience. Conventional gameplay, even when featuring extraordinary abilities of the protagonist, largely draws on classical intuition, shaping the player's reflexes through familiar expectations of motion, action, and consequence. Here, we propose extending these reflexes into the quantum domain by embedding superposition, unitary evolution, quantum gates, and measurement into the game. Central to this approach is a new controller action, the Gate of Fate, which allows players to engage in quantum operations through their gaming decisions. We demonstrate the concept in a Tetris-based prototype, with progressively structured levels that introduce quantum operations and their consequences. We also outline extensions to role playing games, in which the behavior and difficulty of antagonists can respond to player's developing quantum gaming reflexes. By turning abstract quantum concepts into actionable game mechanics, this approach aims to cultivate quantum intuition through play, offering opportunities for both quantum pedagogy and more sophisticated game design.
tldr: The paper proposes a 'Gate of Fate' game mechanic that embeds quantum concepts such as superposition, unitary evolution, quantum gates, and measurement into a Tetris-based prototype to cultivate quantum intuition through play.
motivation: Quantum principles are counterintuitive and hard for beginners to grasp, and conventional video games reinforce classical intuition rather than quantum reflexes, so a game design that makes quantum operations actionable could serve pedagogy.
method: The authors design a controller action ('Gate of Fate') mapped to quantum operations and demonstrate it in a Tetris-based prototype with progressively structured levels, also outlining extensions to role-playing games with quantum-responsive antagonists.
result: A conceptual prototype and design framework are presented; no empirical user study, quantitative learning outcome, or quantum-information-theoretic analysis is reported.
conclusion: Embedding quantum mechanics into game mechanics may help cultivate quantum intuition, offering opportunities for quantum pedagogy and game design, though the work remains conceptual and outside the scope of the researcher's theoretical interests.

title: Hybridization, Degeneracy And Polarization Independence Of Modes In Square Array Of Graphene Disk Resonators With Symmetry C4v
authors: Amanda Evangelista Da Silva Victor Dmitriev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an infinite array of graphene disks in a square unit cell, where every disk of the quadrumer is excited in the dipole regime. Hybridization of plasmonic eigenmodes belonging to different IRREPs of the point group of symmetry C4v is discussed. It is shown that the hybridization of the pair of 1D IRREPs modes A1 and B2 as well as the pair A2 and B1 can exist in this symmetry. For the cell period p0 and the quadrumer period P, the relation P/p0 = 2 defines polarization independence of these pairs of modes. The discussed modes are dark ones and require for their excitation breaking the point symmetry of the quadrumer and, for breaking their degeneracy, i.e. separation in the two pairs, a modification of the discrete translation symmetry, i.e. change the parameter P/p0. The separated modes can be excited by normally incident plane wave with orthogonal polarizations.
tldr: The paper analyzes hybridization, degeneracy, and polarization independence of plasmonic modes in a square array of graphene disk resonators with C4v symmetry.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how symmetry and inter-disk coupling govern the hybridization of plasmonic eigenmodes in graphene metasurfaces.
method: They consider an infinite array of graphene disks in a square unit cell, each disk excited in the dipole regime, and use group theory (C4v irreducible representations) to classify and analyze mode hybridization and degeneracy breaking.
result: Hybridization of A1/B2 and A2/B1 mode pairs is shown to exist, and the condition P/p0 = 2 yields polarization independence for these dark modes, which can be excited by normally incident orthogonally polarized plane waves after symmetry breaking.
conclusion: Symmetry-controlled hybridization provides a route to polarization-independent dark modes in graphene disk arrays, with potential applications in plasmonic metasurfaces.

title: Autonomous Self-harmonic Drift In Langevin Dynamics Causes A Compaction Of Underlying Domain For The Density Of Stochastic Localization
authors: Ken Sekimoto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our recent research on Langevin dynamics with self-harmonic drift and classical spins has revealed a strong connection to ``Stochastic Localization," a concept attracting attention in the fields of mathematical geometry and data science. Roughly speaking, the former can be viewed as a version of the latter in which the [MATH]-dimensional Euclidean space - the domain of the probability distribution function appearing in the latter - is ``compactified'' to the surface of an [MATH]-dimensional sphere. By comparing the two frameworks, we argue that this compactification is a consequence of requiring the drift to be autonomous. The relationship between the two approaches may expand the scope of Stochastic Localization.
tldr: The paper connects Langevin dynamics with autonomous self-harmonic drift to stochastic localization, arguing that the compactification of Euclidean space onto a sphere arises from requiring autonomous drift.
motivation: Stochastic localization is attracting interest in mathematical geometry and data science, and the author aims to clarify its relationship to a class of Langevin dynamics.
method: The author compares Langevin dynamics with self-harmonic drift and classical spins against the framework of stochastic localization.
result: The comparison suggests that the domain compactification to an n-dimensional sphere is a consequence of requiring the drift to be autonomous.
conclusion: The relationship between the two approaches may expand the scope of stochastic localization.

title: Low-loss Amorphous Dielectric Metasurface Mirror For Precision Optical Cavities
authors: Swadha Pandey, Peter Fritschel, Matthew Evans
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the design and experimental realization of a low-loss dielectric metasurface mirror operating at 1064 nm, the primary wavelength of interferometric gravitational-wave detectors. The mirror consists of a single layer of titanium dioxide nanopillars on a glass substrate, achieving high reflectivity via guided-mode resonance. The fabricated mirror has a peak reflectance of 99.10% with a total optical loss of 0.26%, representing, to our knowledge, the highest reflectance and lowest optical loss experimentally demonstrated in a substrate-supported purely amorphous dielectric metasurface mirror operating in the visible to near-infrared. This single-layer metasurface is projected to reduce coating Brownian noise by a factor of 3-5 relative to conventional dielectric Bragg mirrors at comparable reflectivity, which would improve the performance of precision optical cavities currently limited by this noise. These results indicate the potential of dielectric metasurfaces as a platform for next-generation precision measurement systems.
tldr: The authors design and fabricate a low-loss amorphous TiO2 nanopillar metasurface mirror at 1064 nm that achieves 99.10% reflectance with only 0.26% total optical loss, potentially reducing coating Brownian noise in precision optical cavities.
motivation: Conventional dielectric Bragg mirrors used in interferometric gravitational-wave detectors are limited by coating Brownian noise, which constrains the sensitivity of precision optical cavities.
method: A single-layer guided-mode-resonance metasurface consisting of titanium dioxide nanopillars on a glass substrate is designed, fabricated, and optically characterized for reflectance and loss at 1064 nm.
result: The fabricated mirror reaches a peak reflectance of 99.10% and total optical loss of 0.26%, the highest reflectance and lowest loss reported for a substrate-supported purely amorphous dielectric metasurface in the visible-to-near-infrared, with projected 3–5x reduction in coating Brownian noise.
conclusion: Dielectric metasurfaces are identified as a promising platform for next-generation precision measurement systems such as gravitational-wave detectors, though no quantum information or thermodynamics aspects are addressed.

title: A Hyperbolic Bound For File Retrieval In DNA-Based Data Storage
authors: Daniella Bar-Lev Constantinos Vasilios Argyris Vlachos
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In DNA-based storage systems, data are retrieved by sequencing molecules sampled from a DNA pool. We study how the way coding redundancy is shared between files affects their expected retrieval times. Our focus lies on the case of two files that are encoded by a systematic linear code over an arbitrary finite field. We consider the conjecture that the sum obtained by dividing each file dimension by its expected retrieval time is at most one whenever the dimension of at least one file is more than one. For this, we develop a geometric view of the retrieval process. As molecules are sampled, we follow the growing span of the corresponding columns of the generator matrix and track how much of this span comes from each file. Among the samples that enlarge the overall span, this lets us compare those that make progress toward recovering both files with those that make progress toward neither. We call a column mixed if the corresponding encoded symbol combines information from both files. In this work, we sharpen a projection bound and use it to control the effect of mixed columns. We prove the conjecture whenever the total information dimension is at least twice the number of mixed columns plus two. For equal-sized files, this allows up to one fewer mixed column than the dimension of either file and extends the previous result for codes with no mixed columns.
tldr: This paper studies how coding redundancy shared between two files in DNA-based data storage affects their expected retrieval times, using a geometric view and a sharpened projection bound to prove a conjecture under a condition involving mixed columns.
motivation: DNA-based storage systems retrieve data by sampling and sequencing molecules from a pool, and the way redundancy is allocated across files impacts retrieval performance. Understanding this trade-off is important for designing efficient DNA storage architectures.
method: The authors model two files encoded by a systematic linear code over an arbitrary finite field and track the growing span of sampled generator-matrix columns. They introduce the notion of mixed columns and sharpen a projection bound to control the effect of columns that combine information from both files.
result: They prove the conjecture that the sum of each file's dimension divided by its expected retrieval time is at most one whenever the total information dimension is at least twice the number of mixed columns plus two. For equal-sized files, this allows up to one fewer mixed column than the dimension of either file.
conclusion: The work extends previous results for codes with no mixed columns and provides a geometric framework for analyzing file retrieval in DNA-based data storage, though it remains a classical coding-theoretic contribution.

title: Fundamental Limits Of Dynamic Tracking And Communication: A Stationary Policy Formulation
authors: Mohammadreza Bakhshizadeh Mohajer, Luca Barletta, Alex Dytso, Giuseppe Caire
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a dynamic integrated sensing-and-communication problem in which a multi-antenna transmitter communicates with a receiver while simultaneously tracking a moving target governed by a stable Gauss--Markov model. We formulate the sensing--communication trade-off as a rate--distortion problem, where the communication rate is defined through the Verd\'u--Han information spectrum and the sensing distortion is measured by the long-run minimum mean square tracking error in angle and distance. We construct a tractable outer region by lower bounding this distortion through the posterior Cram\'er--Rao bound (PCRB). The control problem is partially observed because the target state is not directly available to the transmitter. We therefore introduce a belief-augmented information state and show, under the stated regularity assumptions, that stationary randomized Markov policies suffice for the covariance-based scalarized problem used in the outer bound. We then derive, under the stated large-block conditions, a Gaussian covariance-control outer bound by showing that, in the large-block regime, the sensing belief transition becomes asymptotically covariance sufficient; consequently, Gaussian signaling with the same stationary covariance policy preserves the stationary PCRB asymptotically while maximizing the communication reward for each transmit covariance. Numerical experiments compare an extended Kalman filter-based achievable frontier with a PCRB-based Gaussian covariance-control outer frontier.
tldr: The paper studies classical dynamic integrated sensing and communication, formulating a rate-distortion trade-off between communication rate and tracking distortion for a moving target under a Gauss-Markov model.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize fundamental limits of joint communication and target tracking when the transmitter has partial observations and must balance communication rate against sensing accuracy.
method: They formulate the problem as a rate-distortion trade-off using the Verdú-Han information spectrum for communication rate and the posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) to lower-bound sensing distortion, then introduce a belief-augmented information state to show that stationary randomized Markov policies suffice for a covariance-based scalarized outer bound, and derive a Gaussian covariance-control outer bound in the large-block regime.
result: They obtain a tractable Gaussian covariance-control outer bound and compare it numerically against an extended Kalman filter-based achievable frontier, showing how Gaussian signaling preserves the stationary PCRB asymptotically under the stated assumptions.
conclusion: Stationary randomized Markov policies are sufficient for the considered outer-bound problem, and the large-block covariance-sufficiency result suggests Gaussian signaling is asymptotically optimal for the sensing-communication trade-off.

title: Tensor-Train Compressed Separable PINNs: A Curvature-Aware Optimization Framework For Parametric PDEs In High Dimensions
authors: Martin Eigel Denis Korolev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a second-order optimization framework for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) applied to high-dimensional parametric partial differential equations (PDEs). The framework is built on the Gauss--Newton pullback metric, which provides an operator-informed notion of curvature in parameter space and connects the method to the broader family of natural gradient schemes. We show that, for coordinate-separable neural architectures and linear differential operators (or linearized operators in the nonlinear case) admitting a finite separable representation, the residual Jacobian inherits a structured separable factorization. This yields an exact compressed formulation of the Gauss--Newton step in a reduced space, without assembling the full residual Jacobian on the exponentially large tensor-product collocation grid. The dimension of the reduced space (the effective compressed dimension) is determined by the local collocation grid sizes, the separable operator structure, and the contraction pattern of the architecture, thereby avoiding dependence on the full tensor-product grid size and replacing dense linear algebra in parameter space by a substantially smaller structured problem. Within our framework, we investigate canonical polyadic and tensor-train parametrizations and derive their full algebraic characterization relevant to the Gauss--Newton method, including the structure of the residual Jacobian, the resulting compressed system, and its effective compressed dimension. Numerical experiments on high-dimensional PDEs, including parametric problems, demonstrate the high efficiency of the proposed compressed Gauss--Newton method, which achieves substantially lower errors than tensor-compressed first-order baselines with orders of magnitude fewer iterations and only a fraction of the computing time.
tldr: The paper develops a tensor-train and canonical polyadic compressed Gauss-Newton optimization framework for separable physics-informed neural networks solving high-dimensional parametric PDEs.
motivation: PINNs struggle in high dimensions because the residual Jacobian and Gauss-Newton linear algebra scale with the exponentially large tensor-product collocation grid, making second-order optimization prohibitive.
method: Leveraging coordinate-separable architectures and finitely separable linear differential operators, the authors exploit a structured separable factorization of the residual Jacobian to derive an exact compressed Gauss-Newton step in a reduced space, with full algebraic characterizations for CP and tensor-train parametrizations.
result: Numerical experiments on high-dimensional parametric PDEs show substantially lower errors than tensor-compressed first-order baselines, with orders of magnitude fewer iterations and a fraction of the computing time.
conclusion: The curvature-aware compressed Gauss-Newton framework makes second-order PINN training tractable in high dimensions by avoiding explicit assembly over the full tensor-product grid.

title: Compressed Sensing With Quantized Tensor Trains (QTTs)
authors: Jingchun Shao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The storage and recovery of a vector of length \(2^d\) can become prohibitively expensive as \(d\) grows, a manifestation of the curse of dimensionality. For certain structured functions and multiscale quantities, the resulting discretized vectors admit compact quantized tensor train (QTT) representations after binary tensorization: a length-\(2^d\) vector is reshaped into a \(d\)-way binary tensor with low tensor-train (TT) rank. Motivated by this construction, we study compressed sensing of tensorized signals that combine bounded TT rank with sparse low-order interaction structure, using randomly sampled Walsh--Hadamard measurements. For this structured model class, we establish a uniform restricted isometry property and derive a measurement condition guaranteeing uniqueness of noiseless recovery. We also propose a structure-aware initializer for the alternating linear scheme (ALS), obtained by projecting the adjoint backprojection onto the low-order interaction space before applying TT-SVD. We prove a uniform initialization error bound whose measurement requirement, for fixed structural parameters, grows polynomially with the tensor order \(d\) rather than with the ambient dimension \(2^d\). Numerical experiments support the predicted RIP and initialization scaling and demonstrate more reliable ALS recovery.
tldr: The paper studies compressed sensing for tensorized signals with bounded quantized tensor-train rank and sparse low-order interactions using random Walsh-Hadamard measurements.
motivation: Storing and recovering a length-2^d vector becomes prohibitively expensive as d grows, but structured functions can admit compact quantized tensor-train representations.
method: The authors establish a uniform restricted isometry property for the structured model class and propose a structure-aware alternating linear scheme initializer via projecting the adjoint backprojection onto the low-order interaction space before TT-SVD.
result: They derive a measurement condition guaranteeing uniqueness of noiseless recovery and prove a uniform initialization error bound whose measurement requirement grows polynomially in d rather than 2^d, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical and numerical support for compressed sensing of QTT-structured signals, improving ALS recovery reliability for high-dimensional tensorized data.

title: Says Block, Still Acts: Why Llm Safety Judgments Fail To Govern Action In Llm Agents
authors: Dongsheng Chen, Xiangyu Zhao, Xin Yao, Xuetao Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents can correctly judge that an action should be blocked while still preferring to take it. We ask why this judgment-action disconnect arises, and whether explicit safety judgment causally governs subsequent action preference. Across three open-weight language models, safety-predictive information remains recoverable from action states, arguing against a simple information-loss account. Instead, the disconnect is better explained by weak coupling between judgment- and action-side causal control: interventions that reliably shift explicit safety judgments toward BLOCK produce much smaller changes in action preference than action-native interventions. This asymmetry persists within a shared judgment-to-action trajectory, where strong upstream control of judgment does not translate into comparably strong downstream control of action preference. Beyond individual intervention directions, judgment- and action-control subspaces overlap only partially, while effective action control remains available in directions orthogonal to the judgment-control subspace. Together, these results distinguish information availability from causal control: an LLM agent can retain the information needed to recognize an action as unsafe without the variables supporting that judgment reliably governing its action preference. For agent safety, this suggests that improving safety recognition or self-critique alone may be insufficient unless safety-relevant computations are also causally coupled to action selection.
tldr: LLM agents can correctly judge an action should be blocked yet still prefer to take it, because judgment-side and action-side causal control are only weakly coupled rather than information being lost.
motivation: Safety training often assumes that accurate safety judgments will govern behavior, but agents exhibit a judgment-action disconnect whose mechanism is unclear and important for agent safety.
method: Across three open-weight LLMs the authors probe whether safety-relevant information persists in action states and perform causal interventions on judgment-side versus action-side directions, comparing how each shifts explicit judgments and action preferences, including within a shared judgment-to-action trajectory.
result: Safety-predictive information remains recoverable from action states, so the disconnect is not information loss; judgment-directed interventions shift BLOCK judgments strongly but change action preference only weakly, and judgment- and action-control subspaces overlap only partially, with effective action control lying in orthogonal directions.
conclusion: Information availability is distinct from causal control in LLM agents, implying that improving safety recognition or self-critique alone may be insufficient unless safety computations are causally coupled to action selection.

title: Combinatorics And Loop Equations For Antisymmetrised And Hermitised Matrix Product Ensembles
authors: Anas. A Rahman Stephane Dartois
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The order [MATH] antisymmetrised matrix product ensemble is represented by the product [MATH], where [MATH] are independent real Ginibre matrices and [MATH] is the elementary antisymmetric matrix, while the order [MATH] Hermitised matrix product ensemble is represented by [MATH], where [MATH] are now independent complex Ginibre matrices and [MATH] is a Hermitian matrix drawn from the Gaussian unitary ensemble. These ensembles have recently been shown to be related to certain Muttalib--Borodin ensembles and integrals of Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber type, thereby motivating further investigation into their eigenvalue statistics. In this work, we construct ribbon graphs and constellations that are enumerated by the mixed cumulants of these ensembles and give loop equation characterisations for the generating functions of said cumulants when [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies antisymmetrised and Hermitised matrix product ensembles using ribbon graphs, constellations, and loop equations to characterize their mixed cumulants and generating functions.
motivation: These random matrix ensembles have recently been linked to Muttalib-Borodin ensembles and Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber integrals, motivating a deeper combinatorial and loop-equation analysis of their eigenvalue statistics.
method: The authors construct ribbon graphs and constellations whose enumeration yields the mixed cumulants of the ensembles, and derive loop equation characterizations for the cumulant generating functions in a limiting regime.
result: They obtain combinatorial expansions and loop equations for the generating functions of mixed cumulants, providing a structural understanding of the eigenvalue statistics of the considered matrix product ensembles.
conclusion: The work contributes to random matrix theory and its combinatorial representation, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dual-Branch Vector-Quantization-Aided Satellite Digital Semantic Communication With Index Compression For High-Resolution Rsi Over Afdm
authors: Jianqiao Chen, Nan Ma, Xiaodong Xu, Tingting Zhu, Huishi Song, Chen Dong, Rui Meng, Wenkai Liu, Ke Peng, Ping Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-resolution remote sensing imagery (RSI) transmission is constrained by satellite-ground bandwidth and channel impairments, yet existing methods struggle to simultaneously achieve extreme compression and robust transmission. To address this, we propose a dual-branch vector-quantization aided satellite digital semantic communication (DVQ-SDSC) framework for RSI transmission over affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), whose bandwidth savings arise from two interrelated aspects. First, at the source-coding level, a dual-branch framework is developed to unify deep joint semantic coding, VQ-aided index transmission, channel estimation and adaption in an end-to-end architecture; departing from symmetric encoder designs, the codec is recast as an asymmetric dual-branch architecture that separately processes the high-frequency residuals and the low-frequency structural semantics, with gated fusion and channel-adaptive reconstruction jointly restoring the semantic content. Second, at the index-coding level, we develop a principal component analysis (PCA)-aided codebook reordering to align index topology with latent correlations, and devise group differential pulse-code modulation (G-DPCM) to encode prediction residuals rather than absolute indices, lowering the index bitrate while locally isolating clipping and channel errors. A two-stage training strategy further decouples channel impairments from the semantic codec. FAIR1M experiments over 3GPP NTN-TDL-D demonstrate that DVQ-SDSC with G-DPCM index coding outperforms the conventional JPEG-LDPC scheme at the base rate of 0.0625 bits per pixel (BPP), and that G-DPCM applies directly to the trained codec without retraining, yielding additional index compression at no extra cost.
tldr: The paper proposes a dual-branch vector-quantization-aided satellite digital semantic communication framework over AFDM for high-resolution remote sensing imagery, with PCA-based codebook reordering and G-DPCM index compression.
motivation: High-resolution remote sensing imagery transmission is limited by satellite-ground bandwidth and channel impairments, and existing methods cannot simultaneously achieve extreme compression and robust transmission.
method: The framework uses an asymmetric dual-branch semantic codec separating high-frequency residuals and low-frequency structural semantics, gated fusion, channel-adaptive reconstruction, PCA-aided codebook reordering, and group differential pulse-code modulation for index compression over AFDM.
result: FAIR1M experiments over 3GPP NTN-TDL-D show DVQ-SDSC with G-DPCM outperforms conventional JPEG-LDPC at 0.0625 BPP, and G-DPCM applies to the trained codec without retraining for additional index compression.
conclusion: The proposed method enables bandwidth-efficient and robust satellite semantic communication for remote sensing imagery, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Absolutely Continuous Convolutions And Projections Of Fractal Measures
authors: Amir Algom, Federico Rodriguez Hertz, Zhiren Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general criterion for establishing absolute continuity of convolutions of fractal measures on the line, and more generally of prescribed line projections of fractal measures in the plane. The crucial new ingredient is exact scaling covariance of the \(L^1\)-norm of Littlewood-Paley pieces of the projected measure, under affine renormalization. We apply this criterion in three key settings. First, we show that the convolution of two measures on the line is absolutely continuous whenever their dimensions sum to more than one, provided one is a self-conformal measure whose defining IFS is not \(C^2\)-conjugate to linear, and the other is either self-conformal or Ahlfors--David regular. Second, we show that every line projection of a planar complex-analytic self-conformal measure of dimension greater than one is absolutely continuous, under natural nonlinearity and nondegeneracy assumptions. Finally, we show that every line projection of a planar self-affine measure is absolutely continuous, under natural irreducibility and proximality assumptions, whenever the correlation dimension of the measure and the Frostman dimension of its Furstenberg measure sum to more than two.
tldr: The paper develops a general criterion for absolute continuity of convolutions and line projections of fractal measures, based on exact scaling covariance of Littlewood-Paley L1-norms under affine renormalization.
motivation: Understanding when convolutions or projections of fractal (self-conformal, self-affine, Ahlfors-David regular) measures become absolutely continuous is a central question in geometric measure theory and harmonic analysis.
method: The authors introduce exact scaling covariance of the L1-norm of Littlewood-Paley pieces of the projected measure under affine renormalization, and apply this criterion to three settings: convolutions of self-conformal measures, line projections of complex-analytic self-conformal measures, and line projections of self-affine measures.
result: They prove absolute continuity of convolutions when dimensions sum above one (with nonlinearity assumptions), of all line projections of planar complex-analytic self-conformal measures of dimension > 1, and of line projections of planar self-affine measures when correlation and Frostman dimensions sum above two.
conclusion: The work provides a unified, technically deep framework for absolute continuity of fractal measure convolutions and projections, advancing pure geometric measure theory with no apparent connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Soft Separation For Adaptive Robust Optimization
authors: Ruiwei Jiang Qingyuan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an algorithmic framework for solving adaptive robust optimization with provable guarantees on both tractability and solution accuracy. The framework introduces soft separation, a probabilistic mechanism for identifying worst-case uncertainty realizations via a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain. Rather than solving an exact separation problem in each iteration, which is intractable in general, the chain carries adversarial information across iterations, co-evolves with the optimization iterates, and recovers exact separation at terminal iterates with high probability. For continuous first-stage (here-and-now) decisions, we design a first-order method that uses soft separation to produce adaptive gradient estimates. Notably, we prove polynomial-time convergence in expectation to the global optimum. For mixed-integer here-and-now decisions, we embed soft separation within a branch-and-cut framework to generate valid cuts for the robust objective and obtain a high-probability certificate of global optimality. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods scale favorably with problem dimension and scenario size relative to state-of-the-art approaches. The instances and code are available online at [URL].
tldr: The paper introduces soft separation, a probabilistic Markov-chain mechanism for adaptive robust optimization that enables tractable first-order and branch-and-cut methods with convergence guarantees.
motivation: Exact separation in adaptive robust optimization is generally intractable, motivating a framework that can identify worst-case uncertainty realizations approximately while preserving solution accuracy.
method: The authors use a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain to carry adversarial information across iterations, co-evolving with optimization iterates and recovering exact separation with high probability at terminal iterates; they embed it in first-order and branch-and-cut algorithms.
result: They prove polynomial-time convergence in expectation to the global optimum for continuous first-stage decisions and obtain a high-probability global optimality certificate for mixed-integer cases, with numerical experiments showing favorable scaling.
conclusion: Soft separation provides a principled and scalable approach to adaptive robust optimization, but it is an operations research and optimization contribution rather than one aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Meromorphic Open-string Vertex Algebras And Twisted Modules From Courant Algebroids
authors: Fei Qi Qixuan Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a sheaf of [MATH]-graded meromorphic open-string vertex algebras from a transitive Courant algebroid [MATH] equipped with a generalized metric and a chosen generalized Levi-Civita connection on a smooth manifold. Using a holonomy principle for transitive anchored bundles, we realize these algebras as parallel sections of a tensor algebra bundle built from bosonic-fermionic affinizations of [MATH]. For even-rank [MATH] with suitable Clifford module bundle data, we construct a sheaf of canonically twisted modules containing the canonical weighted spinor bundle in weight zero. The associative algebra of parallel tensors acts on spinor sections through iterates of an [MATH]-connection combining covariant differentiation and Clifford multiplication, with mixed terms incorporating the action of the bosonic connection on fermionic tensors. Distinguished states built from the inverse Courant pairing and inverse generalized metric give vertex-operator components, acting on embedded spinor sections as the canonical Dirac generating operator, its formal adjoint, and their anticommutator, the generalized Hodge Laplacian. In the exact Courant case with three-form [MATH] and the exterior algebra Clifford module, the operators specialize to [MATH], its adjoint, and the twisted Hodge Laplacian, reducing to the ordinary de Rham and Hodge operators when [MATH]. This extends the vertex-operator realization of geometric differential operators from functions to weighted spinors and differential forms, within the program of studying two-dimensional supersymmetric nonlinear sigma models.
tldr: The paper constructs sheaves of meromorphic open-string vertex algebras and twisted modules from transitive Courant algebroids with generalized metrics and connections.
motivation: It aims to extend vertex-operator realizations of geometric differential operators from functions to weighted spinors and differential forms, within the study of two-dimensional supersymmetric nonlinear sigma models.
method: Using a holonomy principle for transitive anchored bundles, the authors build these algebras as parallel sections of tensor algebra bundles from bosonic-fermionic affinizations, and construct canonically twisted modules via Clifford module bundle data.
result: In the exact Courant case with a three-form and exterior algebra Clifford module, the distinguished vertex operators specialize to the canonical Dirac operator, its adjoint, and the twisted Hodge Laplacian, reducing to ordinary de Rham and Hodge operators when the three-form vanishes.
conclusion: The work provides a vertex-operator framework for geometric differential operators on weighted spinors and differential forms, connecting Courant algebroids to supersymmetric sigma models.

title: Moments Of The Cross-Sectional Siegel-Veech Transfrom
authors: Albert Artiles
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Siegel--Veech transform on the Poinca\'e section for the horocycle flow consisting of lattice surfaces with a visible horizontal holonomy vector of length at most one. We compute its first moment and derive formulas for higher and factorial moments. We emphasize these formulas in the case of the square torus of unit area and, as an application, use its first moment formula to recover the Boca--Zaharescu pair-correlation density for Farey fractions.
tldr: The paper computes first, higher, and factorial moments of the Siegel--Veech transform for horocycle flow on lattice surfaces, with an application to recovering the Boca--Zaharescu pair-correlation density for Farey fractions.
motivation: The Siegel--Veech transform and its moments are central objects in the ergodic theory of translation surfaces and horocycle flows, and explicit moment formulas can reveal arithmetic and statistical properties of lattice surfaces and Farey sequences.
method: The author studies the Siegel--Veech transform on the Poincaré section consisting of lattice surfaces with a visible horizontal holonomy vector of length at most one, computes its first moment, and derives general higher and factorial moment formulas.
result: Explicit moment formulas are obtained, with special emphasis on the unit-area square torus, and the first-moment formula is used to recover the Boca--Zaharescu pair-correlation density for Farey fractions.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic moment analysis of the Siegel--Veech transform and illustrates its utility by re-deriving a known number-theoretic correlation result.

title: Surrogate-Enhanced Fractional Programming For Mimo Device-to-Device Interference Networks
authors: Zihan Jiao, Xinping Yi, Shi Jin, Giuseppe Caire
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interference management in multi-stream multi-input multi-output (MIMO) device-to-device (D2D) networks often leads to weighted sum-rate maximization with sum-log-determinant involving matrix-valued signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios. The state-of-the-art paradigms, including weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) and fractional programming (FP), have achieved tremendous success in link scheduling, power control, and beamforming problems. Recently, an upgraded FP approach, named surrogate-enhanced FP (SEFP) in a scalar form, has attained improved performance in joint uplink scheduling and power control in coordinated multicell SISO networks. The proposed SEFP improves the surrogate construction of the classical Lagrangian dual transform plus quadratic transform for logarithmic fractional objectives with a novel reciprocal-inverse transform (RIT), yet its extension to the matrix form for MIMO settings does not seem straightforward because the matrix ratio and the auxiliary matrix generally do not commute. In this paper, by leveraging mathematical tools from Hermitian functional calculus, we extend RIT to matrix ratios by lifting the scalar RIT along the eigendirections of an auxiliary matrix and recasting the resulting directional construction in an operator form. Following, we develop a matrix SEFP framework for weighted sum-log-determinant maximization. Further, we establish a unified view of SEFP and the recently proposed XMMSE method, specify when the two algorithms attribute to identical minorization-maximization (MM) surrogates and variable update trajectories, and prove XMMSE can be considered as a special case of SEFP under the algorithmic family perspective.Inspired by the unified view, we develop SEFPLinQ for the joint scheduling and beamforming optimization in flexible-association MIMO D2D networks. Numerical results demonstrate consistent performance gains.
tldr: The paper extends surrogate-enhanced fractional programming (SEFP) to matrix-valued MIMO settings using Hermitian functional calculus to solve weighted sum-log-determinant maximization in D2D interference networks.
motivation: Interference management in multi-stream MIMO device-to-device networks leads to non-convex weighted sum-rate maximization, and existing FP/WMMSE methods can be improved by the scalar SEFP approach whose matrix extension is non-trivial due to non-commuting matrix ratios.
method: The authors lift the scalar reciprocal-inverse transform (RIT) along the eigendirections of an auxiliary matrix and recast it in operator form, yielding a matrix SEFP framework, and prove that the recently proposed XMMSE method is a special case under a unified minorization-maximization view.
result: They develop SEFPLinQ for joint scheduling and beamforming in flexible-association MIMO D2D networks, and numerical results show consistent performance gains over state-of-the-art baselines.
conclusion: The work provides a general matrix-form SEFP framework and clarifies its relationship to XMMSE, offering improved algorithms for MIMO D2D interference management, but it lies entirely in classical wireless communication optimization with no quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-system content.

title: Into The Danger Zone: Stable Extrapolation In High-dimensional Function And Operator Learning
authors: Ben Adcock, Simone Brugiapaglia, Xuemeng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization is a central challenge in scientific machine learning. We study regression problems in which the test distribution differs from the training distribution and ask: under what assumptions on the target function or operator is stable extrapolation possible, and how far beyond the training domain can one extrapolate? Existing theory controls the test error through additive penalties measuring the discrepancy between the training and test distributions. Such guarantees show robustness to small distribution shifts, but can very pessimistic in comparison to OOD performance observed empirically. We identify classes of holomorphic functions and operators for which the OOD generalization error converges at algebraic rates even in the presence of large distribution shifts. This phenomenon stems from the increasing smoothness of higher-index coordinates, leading to what we term a `blessing of high dimensionality'. For learning with either polynomials, deep neural networks or deep neural operators, we derive explicit rates for arbitrary test measures supported on suitable domains and quantify how the admissible domain depends on the underlying regularity of the function or operator. Our extrapolation guarantees are independent of the test distribution, depending only on its support. We also present a series of numerical experiments across a range of functions and operators that support the main theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper studies stable out-of-distribution extrapolation in high-dimensional function and operator learning, identifying holomorphic classes where test error converges at algebraic rates under large distribution shifts.
motivation: Out-of-distribution generalization is a central challenge in scientific machine learning, and existing theory often gives pessimistic guarantees under distribution shift.
method: The authors analyze regression for holomorphic functions and operators, derive explicit extrapolation rates for polynomials, deep neural networks, and deep neural operators, and support the theory with numerical experiments.
result: They show a 'blessing of high dimensionality' where OOD error decays algebraically even for large shifts, with guarantees independent of the test distribution depending only on its support.
conclusion: Stable extrapolation is possible for suitable holomorphic functions and operators, with admissible extrapolation domains tied to underlying regularity.

title: GenomeOcean Anywhere: Private WebGPU Inference For Genome MoEs
authors: Fengchen Liu Guang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Genome foundation models are most useful where sequences are generated, yet the largest models need datacenter accelerators and a place to send private DNA. We ask whether a 15-billion-parameter genome mixture-of-experts (MoE) model can instead run on volunteers' web browsers, with the experts spread across many untrusted devices, without changing its predictions and without revealing the sequence to any single device. We build a system in which a trusted coordinator runs attention and routing while browser workers run every expert feed-forward network through hand-written WebGPU kernels, and we protect the expert inputs with real-valued Lagrange coded computing: each worker receives only a Gaussian-padded share, computes the expert's linear maps, and the coordinator decodes from any two of three workers. On GenomeOcean-MoE (8 experts, top-2 routing, 24 layers), the browser path matches native llama.cpp at every quantization level, the distributed path stays at the BF16 numerical noise floor (KL 0.0036 nats per token), and an unfitted latency model predicts decode time within 0.74% (median) under emulated wide-area links. We first show that plaintext expert inputs are not private: a probe recovers the token from a single vector at every depth, and one worker can identify the source genome from 300 unordered tokens with 92% accuracy. With coded experts, an adaptive attacker trained on shares falls to the most-frequent-token baseline, one worker's information about each token is bounded below one bit per forward pass, and the fidelity cost stays below the BF16 noise floor; in Chrome, coded decoding runs at 220 to 376 ms per token, depending on how much of the routing is hidden, and continues without replicas when a worker fails.
tldr: A system for private WebGPU-based distributed inference of a 15-billion-parameter genome mixture-of-experts model using Lagrange coded computing across untrusted browser workers.
motivation: Genome foundation models are most useful at the point of data generation, but large models require datacenter accelerators and raise privacy concerns for DNA sequences.
method: The trusted coordinator runs attention and routing while browser workers execute expert feed-forward networks via hand-written WebGPU kernels, with real-valued Lagrange coded computing and Gaussian-padded shares to protect expert inputs.
result: The browser path matches native llama.cpp across quantization levels, distributed decoding stays within BF16 noise floor (KL 0.0036 nats/token), and privacy improves significantly over plaintext, though latency is 220–376 ms/token in Chrome.
conclusion: Private distributed inference of large genome MoE models is feasible in browsers using coded computing and WebGPU, but the work is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: CipherGenome: Homomorphic Inference For Genomic Mixture-of-Experts
authors: Fengchen Liu Guang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Genome foundation models are growing into sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) networks whose expert weights no longer fit on the machines that hold the sequences, yet sending a private genome to rented accelerators exposes it: we show that a single server hosting one expert recovers the input nucleotides with 99.8% top-1 accuracy. We present CipherGenome, a protocol that keeps the embedding, attention and router of a 15.1B-parameter MoE genome model on a trusted thin client and outsources every expert projection, 95.8% of the parameters, to untrusted and possibly colluding GPU servers under module-LWE encryption. The design exploits three structural facts: expert layers are linear between two SwiGLU gates, expert weights are public, and GPU integer tensor cores can evaluate a ciphertext-weight product exactly modulo [MATH] in a single GEMM. The client evaluates the nonlinearity exactly and re-encrypts with fresh secrets, so no polynomial approximation or bootstrapping is ever needed. On 72 windows from 12 bacterial genomes, encryption adds [MATH] nats per token of KL divergence (95% CI upper bound [MATH]), below a pre-registered non-inferiority margin and indistinguishable from bf16 inference, while the same inversion attack falls to chance level. A reusable public hint cuts end-to-end latency by 3.54 times, wire compression reduces traffic 6.8 times, per-layer padding reduces routing leakage from 54.9% to 8.9% accuracy, and HE-compatible int4 experts remain non-inferior to their plaintext counterparts. Per expert and token, the server-side cost is more than six orders of magnitude below a CKKS baseline.
tldr: CipherGenome is a homomorphic-encryption protocol that outsources linear expert projections of a genomic mixture-of-experts model to untrusted GPU servers while keeping sensitive embeddings, attention, and routing on a trusted client.
motivation: Genome foundation models are becoming sparse mixture-of-experts networks too large for local hardware, but sending private genomes to rented accelerators exposes the input nucleotides to inversion attacks.
method: The protocol keeps nonlinear and routing components client-side and outsources only linear expert projections under module-LWE encryption, exploiting public expert weights and integer tensor-core GEMMs to evaluate ciphertext-weight products exactly without bootstrapping or polynomial approximation.
result: On 72 windows from 12 bacterial genomes, encryption adds negligible KL divergence indistinguishable from bf16 inference, reduces inversion attack success to chance level, and achieves large gains in latency, traffic, and routing leakage over baselines.
conclusion: The work demonstrates practical privacy-preserving inference for genomic MoE models using homomorphic encryption, with server-side costs orders of magnitude below CKKS baselines, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multi-Class, Multi-Tier Network Intrusion Detection: A Comprehensive And Reproducible Benchmark
authors: Yufeng Xin, Bryant Goseland, Mohamed Rahouti
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have dominated Intrusion Detection System (IDS) research in recent years. Unfortunately, many existing studies have produced inflated results and unreliable benchmarks due to critical oversights and mistakes in the ML and DL pipeline, from data collection and labeling to feature engineering and model training and evaluation. CIC-IDS2017 is a standard benchmark for network intrusion detection. Still, many published results on this dataset are difficult to compare due to labeling errors, inconsistent flow extraction, potential leakage, and performance evaluation metrics dominated by benign traffic. In this paper, we present a comprehensive benchmark with corrected PCAP-level labeling and a complete evaluation pipeline with diverse ML models. We evaluate eleven tabular classifiers at three nested levels: binary attack detection, nine-class attack-family attribution, and fifteen-class fine-grained classification. A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM obtains the best fine-tier macro-F1 of 0.955, with coarse and binary macro-F1 scores of 0.980 and 0.999, respectively. We further conducted a feature selection study based on an analysis of feature importance. This comprehensive benchmark pipeline is configurable and open-source, enabling new feature extraction and model plugins for new datasets. Future work should use this pipeline as a reference point for richer features, rare-class analysis, and model generalization towards new datasets and attack classes.
tldr: This paper presents a corrected, open-source benchmark pipeline for multi-class network intrusion detection on CIC-IDS2017, evaluating eleven tabular ML classifiers at binary, coarse (9-class), and fine (15-class) levels.
motivation: Existing ML/DL-based intrusion detection studies on CIC-IDS2017 report inflated and non-comparable results due to labeling errors, inconsistent flow extraction, data leakage, and metrics dominated by benign traffic.
method: The authors rebuild the dataset with corrected PCAP-level labeling and a full reproducible ML pipeline, then evaluate eleven tabular classifiers and feature-importance-based feature selection across three nested classification tiers.
result: A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM achieves macro-F1 scores of 0.955 (fine, 15-class), 0.980 (coarse, 9-class), and 0.999 (binary attack detection).
conclusion: The configurable, open-source benchmark provides a reference point for future work on richer features, rare-class analysis, and generalization to new datasets and attack classes.

title: Quantization Enables Private Dense Retrieval Against Malicious Service Providers
authors: Louis Tremblay Thibault, Sofiane Azogagh, Marc-Olivier Killijian, Ulrich A\"ivodji
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dense retrieval, the key component of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), retrieves the most relevant documents by comparing dense vector representations of queries and passages from a large corpus. In privacy-sensitive applications, the server observes the query and controls which evidence is returned, creating both confidentiality and integrity risks. We formulate private dense retrieval as providing query privacy and retrieval integrity against a malicious server, and develop a two-round cryptographic protocol that provides both guarantees. Our protocol reduces private and verifiable retrieval to multiplication of a committed matrix by an encrypted vector and uses low-bit quantization to make this computation practical. We evaluate the resulting trade-off between cryptographic cost, retrieval quality, and downstream RAG accuracy across six embedding models, four language models, and corpora of up to 2.68 million passages. Our results show that, with a clipped quantizer, three-bit quantization largely preserves retrieval quality and downstream accuracy, while a private query over a corpus the size of a clinical reference requires one to three minutes of server time. These results suggest that private dense retrieval is already practical for moderately sized, privacy-sensitive corpora when minute-scale latency is acceptable.
tldr: The paper develops a two-round cryptographic protocol for private dense retrieval that protects query privacy and retrieval integrity against malicious service providers using low-bit quantization.
motivation: Dense retrieval in RAG applications creates confidentiality and integrity risks because the server sees queries and controls returned evidence, so the authors aim to provide privacy and verifiability against a malicious server.
method: They reduce private and verifiable retrieval to multiplying a committed matrix by an encrypted vector, and use low-bit quantization to make the computation practical across embedding models and corpora.
result: With a clipped quantizer, three-bit quantization largely preserves retrieval quality and downstream RAG accuracy, while a private query over a clinical-reference-sized corpus requires one to three minutes of server time.
conclusion: Private dense retrieval is already practical for moderately sized, privacy-sensitive corpora when minute-scale latency is acceptable.

title: Moment Hierarchy And Exact Steady-state Solutions In A Callaway Lattice Boltzmann Model For Phonon Hydrodynamics
authors: Shimpei Saito
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the moment hierarchy of a Callaway lattice Boltzmann model for phonon hydrodynamics and derive exact steady-state solutions for a driven planar channel with diffuse walls. The collision operator decomposes the population space into conserved, heat-flux, and fast kinetic sectors, whose coupling through streaming determines the transport response. For the two-dimensional, eight-velocity (D2Q8) lattice Boltzmann model, we derive a fully discrete closure that relates the heat flux to transverse kinetic moments. The higher-order transverse kinetic moment contains both a second-difference term and an explicit contribution from the imposed energy drop. Diffuse-wall population constraints then determine the heat-flux and kinetic-moment profiles without fitted parameters. The resulting solution reproduces the numerical bulk moment amplitudes and wall slip, while an exact wall relation separates the contribution of the higher-order moment from deviations from the leading gradient approximation. Finite-wave-number analysis further resolves the collision-sector mixing associated with longitudinal propagation. These results provide a unified description of collision relaxation, the moment hierarchy, and boundary response within the specified discrete model.
tldr: The paper analyzes a Callaway lattice Boltzmann model for classical phonon hydrodynamics, deriving exact steady-state solutions for a driven planar channel using moment hierarchy closure and diffuse-wall boundary conditions.
motivation: Phonon hydrodynamics is important for understanding heat transport in solids, and lattice Boltzmann methods provide a discrete kinetic framework, but their moment closure and boundary treatment require systematic analysis.
method: The collision operator is decomposed into conserved, heat-flux, and fast kinetic sectors; for the D2Q8 lattice, a fully discrete closure relates heat flux to transverse kinetic moments, and diffuse-wall constraints determine profiles without fitted parameters.
result: Exact steady-state solutions reproduce numerical bulk moment amplitudes and wall slip, with an exact wall relation separating higher-order moment contributions from gradient-approximation deviations; finite-wave-number analysis resolves collision-sector mixing for longitudinal propagation.
conclusion: The work provides a unified description of collision relaxation, moment hierarchy, and boundary response within the specified discrete phonon hydrodynamics model.

title: Asymmetric Imaging: Reciprocity Bounds And Manifestations
authors: Romil Audhkhasi, Anna Wirth-Singh, Rose Johnson, Maksym Zhelyeznyakov, Vladimir Yarmolik, Rafael Piestun, Andrea Al\`u, Arka Majumdar, Owen Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent demonstrations of unidirectional imaging using diffractive multilayers have brought a concept akin to optical isolation to imaging, yet the fundamental limits of such asymmetry have remained unknown. Here we develop a general theory of asymmetric imaging in linear, passive, reciprocal optical systems and derive a fundamental bound on the achievable unidirectionality. Reciprocity requires the forward and reverse transmission operators to have identical singular values, a wave-optical analogue of \'etendue equality, with a simple consequence: perfect asymmetry is attainable only for sets of [MATH] orthogonal object patterns, where [MATH] is the number of available object/image modes; for [MATH], the average power asymmetry is bounded by [MATH]. Guided by this result, we present two complementary realizations: refractive imaging systems formed by bulk lenses and stops that attain the half-occupation limit, and a 1 cm-diameter all-silicon metasurface doublet that exhibits asymmetric focusing at 4 [MATH]m while fully complying with Lorentz reciprocity.
