We fabricate the doublet by direct laser writing and experimentally demonstrate its focusing asymmetry. By establishing mechanism-independent limits, our results provide a benchmark and design principle for asymmetric imaging across platforms, with implications for defense, surveillance and secure communications.
tldr: The paper develops a general theory of asymmetric imaging in linear passive reciprocal optical systems and derives fundamental reciprocity bounds on unidirectionality, with experimental demonstrations in refractive and metasurface platforms.
motivation: Recent diffractive multilayer demonstrations of unidirectional imaging suggest optical isolation for imaging, but the fundamental limits of such asymmetry remained unknown.
method: The authors analyze forward and reverse transmission operators in linear passive reciprocal systems to show identical singular values, yielding a bound on achievable asymmetry, and realize refractive and all-silicon metasurface doublet designs.
result: Perfect asymmetry is possible only for a set of orthogonal object patterns; beyond that, average power asymmetry is bounded, and a fabricated 1 cm metasurface doublet exhibits asymmetric focusing at 4 μm while obeying Lorentz reciprocity.
conclusion: The work establishes mechanism-independent limits and design principles for asymmetric imaging, with potential implications for defense, surveillance, and secure communications.

title: Gradient-Free Methods For Stochastic Convex Optimization With Stochastic Functional Constraints
authors: Vadim Abronin, Alexander Gasnikov, Darina Dvinskikh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study convex stochastic optimization with [MATH] expectation constraints, [MATH], when only noisy function values are available. At each call the oracle returns the vector [MATH] at two points, with the same realization of [MATH] at both (two-point feedback). The data may be smooth or nonsmooth, and the objective may be strongly convex. We count three resources separately: [MATH] (batches of queries that can be sent in parallel), , split into calls used for the objective and calls used for the constraints, and that need no new round, such as proximal steps or matrix--vector products with stored Jacobian samples.
tldr: The paper develops gradient-free methods for stochastic convex optimization with stochastic functional constraints under a two-point feedback oracle.
motivation: Many practical optimization problems provide only noisy function values rather than gradients, and may involve stochastic functional constraints that require efficient handling.
method: It uses a two-point feedback oracle where the same random realization is queried at two points, separately counts calls for objective and constraints, and incorporates parallel batches and no-new-round operations.
result: The work establishes resource trade-offs and complexity guarantees for smooth, nonsmooth, and strongly convex settings.
conclusion: The proposed framework advances gradient-free stochastic constrained optimization but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: From Weak To Strong Testing In Gaussian Models
authors: Alexander S. Wein Ansh Nagda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the computational complexity of hypothesis testing in the spiked Wigner model, a prototypical model for detecting low-rank structure in a large random matrix. Below the "BBP" eigenvalue transition, it is expected that strong detection --- with both type I and II errors vanishing --- requires exponential time. Assuming this as a conjecture, we determine the limits of polynomial-time weak detection, exactly characterizing the possible tradeoffs between type I and II errors. Specifically, the optimal tradeoff is achieved by a particular linear spectral statistic. Thus, the question of weak detection is entirely reduced to that of strong detection. The proof builds on ideas of Nagda-Raghavendra (2025) and Moitra-Wein (2025). The low-degree likelihood ratio (LDLR) plays a key role: any test that slightly beats the LDLR can be boosted to have an even higher success probability. This leads us to establish a computational analogue of the Neyman-Pearson lemma for a subclass of additive Gaussian models: for a given super-polynomial runtime, the best possible tradeoff between type I and II errors is either the one achieved by thresholding the LDLR, or the trivial tradeoff that results from strong detection.
tldr: The paper characterizes polynomial-time weak detection limits in the spiked Wigner model, reducing weak detection to a conjecture about exponential-time strong detection.
motivation: Understanding computational complexity of hypothesis testing for low-rank matrix detection is important in high-dimensional statistics and random matrix theory, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors assume a conjecture that strong detection below the BBP transition requires exponential time, then use low-degree likelihood ratio (LDLR) analysis and boosting arguments to determine optimal type I/II error tradeoffs for polynomial-time tests.
result: They prove that the optimal weak detection tradeoff is achieved by a linear spectral statistic, and establish a computational analogue of the Neyman-Pearson lemma for additive Gaussian models under super-polynomial runtime.
conclusion: The work provides a complexity-theoretic reduction from weak to strong detection in Gaussian models, with no direct connection to the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Lexicographic Minimax Load Balancing For T-Adaptive Segment Routing
authors: Kaoutar Bouaachra
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the T-Adaptive Segment Routing, a multi-period optimization problem that emerges in the traffic engineering of core IP/MPLS networks when scheduled maintenance operations are involved. The problem seeks a sequence of Segment Routing (SR) configurations that can adapt to a multi-period scheduled maintenance, while allowing limited number of path reconfigurations between successive time steps. Instead of only minimizing the classical Maximum Link Utilization (MLU) criteria, we propose a more refined lexicographic objective that minimizes the sorted vector of link loads in its entirety, thereby enabling a more efficient resource utilization across all links. To tackle this problem, we develop three exact formulations for solving the resulting lexicographic optimization problem. Among these, the Stela and Carla formulations provide the most favorable computational basis for trajectory-based optimization. We thus develop a trajectory column-generation scheme for these formulations, using pricing oracles that vary from heuristic to exact. Exact pricing gives an exact solution of the LP relaxation of the trajectory master, but it does not itself give a certificate of integer optimality: solving the integer master over the columns generated at the root node only certifies optimality within the generated column pool. To overcome this gap, we incorporate trajectory column generation into a Branch-and-Price framework. The branching rule operates on aggregate variables representing segment usage, which correspond to the original compact routing variables. Thus, Branch-and-Price guarantees global integer optimality for every Stela and Carla rank, and when all ranks are solved to exactness, it guarantees lexicographic optimality of the final solution.
tldr: The paper introduces T-Adaptive Segment Routing, a multi-period traffic-engineering optimization problem for IP/MPLS core networks under scheduled maintenance, solved via lexicographic minimax load balancing and a Branch-and-Price trajectory column-generation scheme.
motivation: Scheduled maintenance in core IP/MPLS networks forces repeated Segment Routing reconfigurations, and classical Maximum Link Utilization minimization is too coarse to capture efficient resource usage across all links.
method: Three exact formulations (notably Stela and Carla) are developed for the lexicographic optimization, combined with trajectory column generation using heuristic-to-exact pricing oracles embedded in a Branch-and-Price framework with branching on aggregate segment-usage variables.
result: Branch-and-Price certifies global integer optimality for each Stela and Carla rank, and solving all ranks to exactness yields lexicographic optimality of the overall SR configuration sequence.
conclusion: Lexicographic minimax optimization with trajectory Branch-and-Price provides a computationally viable and provably optimal approach to multi-period Segment Routing reconfiguration under maintenance constraints.

title: An Energy-Conserving Unstaggered Electromagnetic-Potential Particle-in-Cell Method, Part Ii: Fully Relativistic Formulation With An Adapted Higuera--Cary Pusher
authors: Andrew Christlieb, Luis Chacon, Sining Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a fully relativistic extension of the energy-conserving, unstaggered electromagnetic-potential particle-in-cell method introduced in our earlier nonrelativistic work. As in the nonrelativistic generalized-momentum formulation, the fields are advanced by a Crank--Nicolson discretization of the Lorenz-gauge potential equations, the current is deposited from particle orbits, and charge is advanced through the discrete continuity equation. The new ingredient is a generalized-momentum adaptation of the Higuera--Cary relativistic particle pusher. The vector-potential force is decomposed into an orbit-discrete-gradient part, which enforces the same finite-difference chain rule used in our earlier nonrelativistic formulation, and a skew part, which generates a Higuera--Cary magnetic rotation in mechanical momentum. For prescribed fields and frozen orbit data, this generalized-momentum Higuera--Cary map is a unit-Jacobian conjugacy of the mechanical Higuera--Cary map and preserves particle phase volume in [MATH]. For the fully coupled implicit step, the same orbit data define the current deposit, mesh-to-particle gather, vector-potential chain rule, and relativistic kinetic-energy secant velocity. The resulting particle work cancels the Crank--Nicolson field-energy balance, yielding exact relativistic total-energy conservation up to nonlinear solver tolerance, orbit-quadrature error, and roundoff. A self-adjoint Fourier projection removes modes on even-grid Nyquist planes while preserving the particle--grid work identity. Numerical tests are organized around cold relativistic two-stream and Weibel/filamentation instabilities, with diagnostics for energy drift, Gauss's law, the Lorenz gauge, particle--grid work, and the orbit chain rule.
tldr: The paper presents a fully relativistic, energy-conserving electromagnetic-potential particle-in-cell method using an adapted Higuera--Cary pusher for plasma simulation.
motivation: Existing nonrelativistic energy-conserving PIC schemes need a relativistic extension that maintains exact total-energy balance and charge continuity for high-energy plasma regimes.
method: Fields are advanced via a Crank--Nicolson discretization of the Lorenz-gauge potential equations, currents are deposited from particle orbits with discrete continuity, and a generalized-momentum Higuera--Cary pusher splits the vector-potential force into orbit-discrete-gradient and skew (magnetic rotation) parts, with a self-adjoint Fourier projection removing Nyquist modes.
result: The generalized-momentum Higuera--Cary map is a unit-Jacobian conjugacy preserving phase volume, and the fully coupled implicit step yields exact relativistic total-energy conservation up to solver tolerance, quadrature error, and roundoff, validated on relativistic two-stream and Weibel instabilities.
conclusion: The scheme provides a robust relativistic energy-conserving PIC framework for plasma physics, but it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Approximating Combinatorial Contracts With Arbitrary Costs
authors: Xiaotie Deng, Hanyu Li, Chenghua Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study single-agent combinatorial contracts under linear payments. Under a reward share [MATH], an agent chooses a subset [MATH] of [MATH] hidden actions, generating reward [MATH] at cost [MATH], to maximize [MATH], while the principal receives [MATH]. For nonnegative additive rewards and monotone supermodular costs, D\"utting et al. (SODA 2026) proved an exponential supply-query lower bound for exact optimization and left open whether a representation-independent approximation is possible. We resolve this question in a stronger form, removing all structural assumptions on the cost function: for nonnegative additive rewards, arbitrary normalized nonnegative set costs, and every [MATH], we give a deterministic [MATH]-approximation using [MATH] supply queries, with query complexity independent of numerical bit lengths and breakpoint separation. More generally, the same guarantee and asymptotic query complexity hold for normalized monotone subadditive rewards and arbitrary normalized nonnegative costs under exact best-response and value-query access. The key idea is a cost-independent, reward-side scale certificate. The algorithm tries all singleton rewards as candidate anchors; one of them brackets the optimal retained share within a factor [MATH]. Geometric search and monotonicity of the induced response reward then yield the approximation without enumerating best-response breakpoints.
tldr: This paper studies single-agent combinatorial contracts with arbitrary costs and provides a deterministic approximation algorithm with query complexity independent of numerical precision.
motivation: The authors aim to resolve an open problem from Dütting et al. (SODA 2026) on whether representation-independent approximation is possible for combinatorial contracts when costs are arbitrary, rather than under structural assumptions.
method: The key idea is a cost-independent, reward-side scale certificate: trying all singleton rewards as candidate anchors, then using geometric search and monotonicity of the induced response reward to avoid enumerating best-response breakpoints.
result: For nonnegative additive rewards, arbitrary normalized nonnegative set costs, and any reward share, the paper gives a deterministic approximation using supply queries with query complexity independent of bit lengths and breakpoint separation, and extends the guarantee to monotone subadditive rewards under exact best-response and value-query access.
conclusion: This work removes all structural assumptions on the cost function and resolves the open approximation question in a stronger form for combinatorial contract design.

title: Raising The Bar For Chinese Adolescent Llm Safety: A Culturally-Grounded, Fine-Grained Benchmark
authors: Jinxiang Wang, Yifan Liu, Jing Tan, Xiangyu Zhao, Xin Yao, Xuetao Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety risks in conversations with adolescents are not always explicit. A request may appear harmless unless a model considers the user's age, circumstances, and earlier turns. Existing Chinese safety benchmarks mainly target general users and give limited attention to adolescent safety. Single-turn tests also miss risks that emerge over several turns. QH-Bench is a Chinese-language benchmark for adolescent content safety, with scenarios grounded in Chinese social and cultural settings. The single-turn track contains 715 test items organized into 10 risk domains, 50 subdomains, and 143 fine-grained risk scenarios. The multi-turn track contains 100 four-turn trajectories in a balanced 10-by-10 design that combines the same ten domains with ten cross-turn mechanisms. Both tracks use the same five-level safety-helpfulness scale and automatic judge, with track-specific criteria. Evaluation of 13 open-weight models identifies offline-contact scenarios as a shared weakness. Every model receives negative scores on more than half of the items involving offline meetings with online contacts, unfamiliar groups, and adults. This includes InternLM2.5-20B, the single-turn leader; negative scores indicate responses that partially or clearly facilitate risk. GLM-4-32B, the multi-turn leader, receives negative scores on 60% of complete trajectories in which users build relationships before invoking loyalty or confidentiality. These findings identify two priorities for the evaluated models: handling adolescent offline-contact risks and maintaining safety boundaries under relational pressure. Leading aggregate scores do not establish that these specific weaknesses have been resolved.
tldr: QH-Bench is a culturally grounded Chinese-language benchmark for evaluating adolescent content safety in LLMs across single-turn and multi-turn conversations.
motivation: Existing Chinese safety benchmarks focus on general users and single-turn tests, missing adolescent-specific risks and multi-turn dangers that emerge through relationship building and offline contact.
method: The benchmark contains 715 single-turn items across 10 risk domains, 50 subdomains, and 143 fine-grained scenarios, plus 100 four-turn trajectories balanced across domains and cross-turn mechanisms, evaluated using a five-level safety-helpfulness scale and automatic judge.
result: Evaluation of 13 open-weight models reveals offline-contact scenarios as a shared weakness, with every model scoring negatively on more than half of items involving offline meetings, unfamiliar groups, and adults; GLM-4-32B fails on 60% of relationship-pressure trajectories.
conclusion: The findings highlight two priorities for Chinese adolescent LLM safety: handling offline-contact risks and maintaining safety boundaries under relational pressure, showing that aggregate scores can mask specific weaknesses.

title: Similarity Is Not Validity: Defending Llm Semantic Caches Against Poisoning
authors: Zihan Zhang, Shuangjie Yao, Zesen Liu, Zhixiang Zhang, Wai Ip Lai, Dung Hiu Hilton Yeung, Chun Kit Zhang, Fuchen Ma, Yuanyuan Yuan, Yu Jiang, Dongdong She
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic caches reduce LLM serving costs by reusing previously generated answers for semantically similar queries. However, retrieval is based solely on embedding similarity between the incoming query and cached queries. This design enables cache poisoning: an attacker can cache a malicious response under a query with high cosine similarity to benign requests. The vulnerability stems from a gap between retrieval similarity and answer validity. From an information-bottleneck perspective, query embeddings can lose information needed to distinguish valid from invalid cache hits, which limits any matching algorithm that uses only these embeddings. We propose a novel defense that recovers this necessary information from the raw text of the cache key. Across poisoning attacks, adversarial queries share a rewrite-residual structure: they pair a rewrite of the target query with residual content. The rewrite maintains high similarity, while the residual elicits the malicious response. Deleting the residual makes the remaining rewrite more similar to the incoming query. We exploit this structure using Deletion Gain to search shortened variants of the cached query for similarity gains, and an Answer Check to test whether the removed text contributes to the stored answer. We prove that Deletion Gain stays positive when a deletion leaves text close enough to the rewrite, and we search for such deletions with a sliding window. Across three poisoning attack classes, our defense blocks 82.0% to 98.2% of poisoned entries at a 5% false-positive rate, with negligible serving overhead.
tldr: The paper defends LLM semantic caches against poisoning attacks by exploiting the rewrite-residual structure of adversarial queries via a Deletion Gain heuristic and an Answer Check.
motivation: Semantic caches reuse answers based on embedding similarity alone, creating a gap between retrieval similarity and answer validity that attackers can exploit to inject malicious cached responses.
method: Framed through an information-bottleneck lens, the authors recover validity information from the raw cache-key text by searching shortened query variants that yield similarity gains (Deletion Gain) and verifying whether removed text contributed to the stored answer (Answer Check), implemented with a sliding window.
result: Across three poisoning attack classes, the defense blocks 82.0% to 98.2% of poisoned entries at a 5% false-positive rate with negligible serving overhead.
conclusion: Similarity is not validity; recovering information from raw text rather than embeddings alone yields a practical, theoretically motivated defense for LLM semantic caches.

title: Adversarial Debiasing Of Machine Learning Models For Enhanced Network Security Against DDoS Attacks
authors: Aadith Sukumar, Isha Singh, Devershika Mohane, Ankit Mukherjee, Ankush Dutta, Rahee Walambe, Ketan Kotecha
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed Denial of Service attacks are a growing threat to network infrastructure, and new techniques, including the use of generative AI, make them harder to detect. Traditional detection systems, such as rule based firewalls, often fail to identify these evolving attack patterns. In this study, we propose a new method for detecting DDoS attacks by combining synthetic data generation using Generative Adversarial Networks with a Random Forest classifier. The GAN generated data showed 80.3 percent cosine similarity to real traffic, which helped the model learn underlying traffic patterns more effectively. To address imbalances in the data, especially in packet related features, we applied adversarial debiasing. This reduced the model's sensitivity to skewed distributions in variables such as forward and backward packet counts and total byte lengths. Our results show that models trained on a mix of synthetic and real data achieved significantly better performance: 99.98 percent accuracy on benchmark data and a 22.60 percent improvement when tested on previously unseen synthetic traffic. This suggests that the method can generalize well across different traffic scenarios and adapt quickly to new types of attacks. The proposed approach not only improves DDoS detection but also provides a scalable foundation for security models that account for bias and benefit from data augmentation. Our findings show that combining GANs with adversarial debiasing can lead to more robust and effective DDoS mitigation, supporting the further development of machine learning based cyber security.
tldr: The paper proposes combining GAN-based synthetic traffic generation with adversarial debiasing and a Random Forest classifier to improve DDoS attack detection in network security.
motivation: DDoS attacks are increasingly difficult to detect using traditional rule-based firewalls, especially as generative AI enables more evasive attack patterns, and imbalanced packet-level traffic data further degrades classifier reliability.
method: They generate synthetic DDoS traffic using a Generative Adversarial Network, measure similarity to real traffic, and train a Random Forest classifier on mixed synthetic and real data while applying adversarial debiasing to reduce sensitivity to skewed packet-count and byte-length features.
result: The synthetic data achieved 80.3% cosine similarity to real traffic, and the debiased model trained on mixed data reached 99.98% accuracy on benchmark data and improved by 22.60% on unseen synthetic traffic.
conclusion: The authors conclude that combining GAN-based augmentation with adversarial debiasing can produce more robust and generalizable DDoS detection models, offering a scalable direction for security-focused machine learning.

title: From Reconnaissance To Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization And Game Theoretic Containment In Modern Enterprise Attack
authors: Shadeeb Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern Security Operations Centers struggle with delayed manual incident response, enabling adversaries to advance through the Cyber Kill Chain during early stage reconnaissance. While classical game theoretic defense models optimize strategic resource allocation, they rely on static utility matrices that fail to adapt to dynamic telemetry. This paper presents an integrated, metrics driven decision engine that bridges quantitative risk parameterization and continuous automated response time. Common Vulnerability Scoring Systems exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and evaluate defender log distributions via Factor Analysis of Information Risk Monte Carlo simulations. Real time SIEM logs streams are modeled as Poisson process arrival rates, dynamically updating defender posterior threat belief through sequential Bayesian filtering. A closed form threshold is derived by framing the interaction as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the expected unmitigated risk exceeds proactive containment cost. Parameterized against empirical data from the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment cyber incident, simulation results demonstrate that the engine suppresses transient background noise while triggering automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of adversarial probing. Multi parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the decision boundary dynamically adjusts to live perimeter vulnerability, offering a control theoretic foundation for sub minute automated threat containment.
tldr: The paper proposes a metrics-driven decision engine combining quantitative risk parameterization and dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game theory to automate enterprise incident containment within seconds.
motivation: Security operations centers face delayed manual response to early-stage reconnaissance, while classical game-theoretic defense models use static utility matrices that cannot adapt to real-time telemetry.
method: CVSS exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and defender log distributions via FAIR Monte Carlo simulations, with SIEM logs modeled as Poisson arrivals and defender beliefs updated through sequential Bayesian filtering; a closed-form containment threshold is derived from a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game.
result: Simulations parameterized with the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment incidents show the engine suppresses transient noise and triggers automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of probing, with sensitivity analysis confirming dynamic adjustment to live vulnerability.
conclusion: The framework offers a control-theoretic foundation for sub-minute automated threat containment in enterprise environments, though it is outside the scope of quantum information science.

title: Matrix-Vector Complexity Of Low-Rank Approximation
authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish matching polynomial query bounds for low-rank approximation from exact matrix--vector products. Given an unknown matrix [MATH], at each step a randomized algorithm chooses either [MATH] and receives [MATH], or [MATH] and receives [MATH]. The choice may depend measurably on all previous queries and replies and on the algorithm's private randomness; each vector product costs one query. The output is a rank-[MATH] right projector with Schatten-[MATH] residual at most [MATH] times optimal. Write [MATH] and let [MATH] denote the worst-case query budget for success probability [MATH] on every input. For every [MATH], [MATH]. These bounds have universal constants and allow [MATH] to vary with the problem parameters, identifying the transition at [MATH]. A complementary result for each fixed [MATH] gives [MATH], with constants and an accuracy threshold that may depend on [MATH]. Together, the results recover this fixed-norm rate for every fixed finite [MATH], supplying the multiplicative rank dependence missing from previous lower bounds. Tildes suppress logarithmic factors. The proof extends adaptive Wishart deferred decisions to a rectangular factor with a [MATH]-dimensional nullspace. Posterior overlap gives a short fixed-norm argument, while persistence of small compression eigenvalues controls growing [MATH] and the spectral endpoint. Exact range recovery handles target costs of order [MATH]; the Wishart family covers the remaining regimes.
tldr: The paper establishes matching polynomial query bounds for low-rank approximation when an algorithm can only access an unknown matrix through exact matrix-vector products.
motivation: Low-rank approximation is a fundamental primitive in numerical linear algebra and machine learning, but its query complexity under the matrix-vector access model was not tightly characterized, especially with respect to rank dependence and norm scaling.
method: The authors prove upper and lower bounds on the worst-case number of matrix-vector queries needed to output a rank-k projector achieving a Schatten-p residual within a constant factor of optimal, extending adaptive Wishart deferred-decision techniques to a rectangular factor with a k-dimensional nullspace.
result: They obtain matching polynomial bounds for every p and adaptive k, identifying a transition at p = 2, and recover the fixed-norm rate for every fixed finite p while supplying the multiplicative rank dependence missing from earlier lower bounds.
conclusion: The work resolves the query complexity of low-rank approximation under exact matrix-vector products, but it is a purely classical algorithmic/complexity result with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: DNN-Assisted Near-Optimal Codebook Design For Uplink Scma Schemes Over Rician Fading Channels
authors: Wasif Ali, Yen-Ming Chen, Fan-Shuo Tseng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA) is a promising non-orthogonal multiplexing technique for enhancing connectivity and spectral efficiency in next-generation communication networks. This paper proposes near-optimal uplink SCMA codebook designs based on a novel deep neural network (DNN)-assisted framework. The DNN is trained in an unsupervised manner, with a loss function derived from the structural characteristics of the generated codebooks, thereby eliminating the need for labeled training data. Based on error-probability analysis, Rician-factor-dependent design criteria are derived for uplink Rician fading and used to formulate the loss function. The resulting criteria naturally encompass AWGN and Rayleigh fading as limiting cases, providing a unified framework for codebook design. Moreover, upper and lower bounds on the average mutual information (AMI) are derived, providing an information-theoretic interpretation of the PEP-based criterion and establishing its asymptotic consistency with the AMI-lower-bound-based criterion in the high-SNR regime. The analysis further reveals how the dominant design factors evolve as the channel transitions from Rayleigh fading to AWGN. Numerical results show that the proposed near-optimal codebooks achieve significant performance gains over representative benchmark schemes across a wide range of Rician factors and exhibit excellent error-rate performance in the error-floor region, making them particularly attractive for ultra-reliable applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep neural network-assisted framework for near-optimal uplink SCMA codebook design over Rician fading channels.
motivation: SCMA is a promising non-orthogonal multiplexing technique for improving connectivity and spectral efficiency in next-generation communication networks, motivating better codebook designs.
method: An unsupervised DNN is trained using a loss function derived from error-probability analysis and Rician-factor-dependent design criteria, with average mutual information bounds providing an information-theoretic interpretation.
result: Numerical results show the proposed near-optimal codebooks achieve significant performance gains over benchmark schemes across various Rician factors and exhibit excellent error-rate performance in the error-floor region.
conclusion: The proposed DNN-assisted codebook design offers a unified framework for uplink SCMA and is particularly attractive for ultra-reliable communication applications.

title: A Tree-Based Localized Reduced Basis Method For Parametrized Parabolic PDEs
authors: Diane Guignard Mohamed Barakat
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a localized reduced basis method for parametrized parabolic partial differential equations based on an adaptive partitioning of the parameter domain using hierarchical binary trees. A POD-Greedy procedure is employed to construct reduced spaces associated with each parameter subdomain. A certified error estimator is derived from an inf-sup stability analysis and shown to be equivalent to the underlying approximation error. This equivalence, together with suitable regularity assumptions on the parameter-to-solution map, enables a rigorous convergence analysis and is used to derive a strategy for selecting the number of POD modes to retain in each local reduced space. Numerical experiments for a parametrized convection--diffusion problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and confirm the predicted convergence behavior.
tldr: The paper introduces a tree-based localized reduced basis method for parametrized parabolic PDEs, with certified error estimators and a rigorous convergence analysis.
motivation: Parametrized parabolic PDEs are expensive to solve repeatedly across large parameter domains, motivating local reduced-order models that adaptively partition the parameter space.
method: An adaptive hierarchical binary tree partitions the parameter domain, POD-Greedy constructs local reduced spaces, and an inf-sup-based certified error estimator guides mode selection.
result: The certified estimator is proven equivalent to the true approximation error, enabling rigorous convergence analysis and a principled criterion for choosing the number of POD modes per subdomain.
conclusion: Numerical experiments on a parametrized convection-diffusion problem confirm the effectiveness of the approach and the predicted convergence behavior.

title: Voronoi-Markov Chain And Spatial Entropy For Point Pattern Analysis
authors: James C. Mathews Jr., Francisco Couzo, Aleksandr Petrov, Avijit Chatterjee, Saad Nadeem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we revisit the concept of entropy in the spatial context with the aim of deriving computable and interpretable metrics for point pattern analysis in domains such as histopathology. We discuss stochastic point process assumptions like Poisson homogeneity and Simple Sequential Inhibition (SSI) and review established results for Voronoi and Delaunay tilings of point sets for their potential to provide null distributions for rigorous empirical hypothesis testing. We present (1) a novel "dense basin entropy" defined in terms of the Ord distribution supported on Voronoi basins, which is shown to be sensitive to clustering, and (2) a related Markov chain designed as a simplification or approximation of Brownian motion in the underlying planar domain. We investigate bounds on the dense basin entropy in the SSI regime and in empirical data, and show that the entropy rate and spectral gap of the Markov chain lead to sharp discrimination metrics. Finally, we demonstrate a generalization to multiple-set analysis via aggregation of one set over the Markov invariant measure for another. Simulations and experiments in histopathology show that our proposed metrics offer insights complementary to other instantiations of entropy in spatial analysis. The code can be found on our SMProfiler GitHub: [URL].
tldr: The paper introduces a novel dense basin entropy and a Voronoi-Markov chain framework for spatial point pattern analysis, with applications in histopathology.
motivation: The authors aim to derive computable and interpretable entropy-based metrics for spatial point patterns, moving beyond classical stochastic point process assumptions.
method: They define dense basin entropy using the Ord distribution over Voronoi basins and design a Markov chain approximating Brownian motion in the plane, investigating bounds under Simple Sequential Inhibition and empirical data.
result: The proposed metrics are sensitive to clustering, and the entropy rate and spectral gap of the Markov chain yield sharp discrimination; simulations and histopathology experiments show complementary insights to existing spatial entropy measures.
conclusion: The work provides new spatial entropy and Markov chain tools for point pattern analysis, with potential utility in histopathology and other spatial domains.

title: Design And Implementation Of Interactive Videos In Undergraduate Transnational Education
authors: Ebru Burcu Dimitrios Chiotis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing development of online educational video resources over the past two decades, has significantly reshaped university students' self-regulated study approaches and influenced diverse ways of learning. Within an environment of abundantly and publicly available online resources, educators cannot always control which materials students choose to supplement their study. Consequently, considerable deviations are likely to be present between the taught content by the educator and an arbitrary online educational video the student watches, in terms of terminology, notation and methods, especially in mathematical sciences. These deviations can be even more considerable when Transnational Education (TNE) students incorporate native language resources to comprehend the material. This paper presents the design, creation and implementation of interactive video resources produced in alignment with established pedagogical frameworks to support an undergraduate TNE mathematics module.
tldr: The paper describes the design, creation, and implementation of interactive video resources for an undergraduate transnational education mathematics module.
motivation: Online educational videos are widely used by students, but deviations in terminology, notation, and methods between taught content and external resources can hinder learning, especially for transnational education students who may use native-language materials.
method: The authors designed interactive videos aligned with established pedagogical frameworks and implemented them to support an undergraduate transnational education mathematics module.
result: The paper presents the design and implementation process, likely including practical considerations and outcomes from deploying the interactive video resources in a TNE mathematics context.
conclusion: Interactive video resources can be structured pedagogically to better align with course content and support transnational education students in mathematics, though the work is specific to educational technology rather than quantum information or related fields.

title: On The Lack Of Periodicity Of Walker Satellite Constellation Routing Tables
authors: Fran\c{c}ois Baccelli Chang-Sik Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a referential that rotates with Earth, the dynamics of the configurations of satellites in a Delta Walker constellation can be analyzed as a dynamical system as a function of a translation on the torus. This paper extends this type of analysis to routing over a Walker constellation, leveraging fixed ground relays. It considers any deterministic, time-invariant routing rule on such a collection of satellites and relays. The main object of interest is the routing table associated with this rule, which specifies, for all source-destination pairs, a route made of satellites and relays between them, for instance the shortest, together with angular information on next hop at each step of the route, which is essential for beamforming in this context. The main result is that, for each such routing rule, the routing table inherits the dichotomy of the torus flow: when the ratio of the Earth-spin and satellite angular speeds is rational, the routing table process is periodic with the same period as the constellation. When it is irrational, the table is non periodic but admits ergodic long-run averages which can be computed as ensemble averages w.r.t. an explicit invariant measure. Simulations with mixed satellite--gateway greedy routing illustrate these findings in terms of both temporal and spectral properties of the Walker routing table time series. The paper also discusses how to define metrics that cope with such non periodic fluctuations when present. This is illustrated by a comparison of the round-trip times between two far away cities as offered by a Walker constellation using greedy routing on one side, and by the currently available terrestrial fiber on the other side. It is shown how ergodicity can be used to make this comparison between the time varying instantaneous round trip times of the constellation and the constant round trip time of the fiber network meaningful.
tldr: The paper analyzes routing tables for Delta Walker satellite constellations, showing they are periodic when Earth-spin to satellite angular speed ratio is rational and ergodic otherwise, with an invariant measure for long-run averages.
motivation: Walker constellations are increasingly used for global communication, and routing over them involves time-varying topology; the authors aim to characterize the temporal behavior of routing tables to enable meaningful performance metrics.
method: They model the constellation in an Earth-rotating frame as a torus flow, consider deterministic time-invariant routing rules with fixed ground relays, and derive periodicity or ergodicity of the routing table process; simulations with greedy routing illustrate temporal and spectral properties.
result: For rational speed ratios, routing tables are periodic; for irrational ratios, they are non-periodic but have computable ergodic averages via an explicit invariant measure, which allows comparison of satellite and terrestrial fiber round-trip times.
conclusion: The work provides a dynamical-systems framework for understanding satellite routing tables and suggests metrics that accommodate non-periodic fluctuations, applicable to Walker constellation network design.

title: Cardinality-Constrained Randomized Assortments With Balanced Market Share
authors: Xiaotie Deng, Hanyu Li, Chenghua Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assortment optimization asks a seller which of [MATH] products to display to each customer. Under the multinomial-logit (MNL) model, a revenue-maximizing policy may concentrate most purchases on only a few products. Balanced market share (BMS) limits this disparity by requiring every product to receive either zero aggregate sales or at least an [MATH]-fraction of the largest product's sales. We study randomized BMS under a per-assortment cardinality constraint: every displayed assortment contains at most [MATH] products, although the seller may rotate a larger catalog across customers. This couples per-realization feasibility with aggregate balance over an exponential policy space. We resolve the model on all three algorithmic fronts. First, reweighting assortments by their MNL denominators turns the cardinality restriction into a single uniform-matroid rank inequality, yielding an exact compact sales-space formulation in which every feasible sales vector can be implemented by a policy supported on [MATH] assortments. Second, deciding whether there exists a feasible policy attaining a given revenue target is NP-complete even for [MATH] and [MATH], whereas optimization is polynomial-time solvable once the set of products with positive sales is prescribed. Third, despite this hardness, BMS confines all positive sales to one multiplicative band, and a geometric scale search combined with a standard multiple-choice-knapsack dynamic program yields an FPTAS. For every [MATH], it achieves at least a [MATH] fraction of the optimal expected revenue, preserves BMS and per-assortment cardinality exactly, and outputs a rational policy supported on [MATH] assortments.
tldr: This paper studies cardinality-constrained randomized assortments under balanced market share in the multinomial-logit model, providing a compact formulation, hardness results, and an FPTAS.
motivation: Revenue-maximizing policies under MNL can concentrate sales on few products, and balanced market share constraints limit this disparity, but per-assortment cardinality constraints couple feasibility with aggregate balance over an exponential policy space.
method: The authors reweight assortments by MNL denominators to reduce the cardinality restriction to a uniform-matroid rank inequality, yielding an exact compact sales-space formulation, then analyze complexity and design an FPTAS via geometric scale search and multiple-choice-knapsack dynamic programming.
result: They obtain an exact compact formulation, show that deciding feasibility for a revenue target is NP-complete even for small parameters, prove polynomial solvability when the positive-sales support is fixed, and give an FPTAS achieving at least a 1-epsilon fraction of optimal revenue while preserving BMS and cardinality exactly.
conclusion: The paper resolves algorithmic aspects of cardinality-constrained randomized BMS assortments, but its operations research and algorithmic game theory topics are unrelated to the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: The Exact Welfare Guarantee Of Fixed-Price Bilateral Trade
authors: Tingyi Lin, Yichen Shi, Ke Dong, Jiazhuo Li, Shawn Yu, Huanxi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A seller and a buyer with independent private values can trade only at a posted price. We determine the worst case of this mechanism exactly: the best posted price always guarantees a [MATH] fraction of first-best welfare, where [MATH] is the root of an explicit equation, the worst-case buyer is unique up to scaling, and no pair of distributions attains the worst case. This closes the gap [MATH] left by a line of work from SODA 2016 through two STOC 2023 papers and AAAI 2026. The proof is an explicit certificate of optimality: after one change of variables, the gap between the optimal value and that of any buyer distribution is a sum of nonnegative integrals, as in a linear-programming dual, and equality identifies the worst-case shape. The certificate also gives the complete tradeoff between gains from trade and the seller's initial welfare: when first-best gains from trade are a fraction [MATH] of initial seller welfare, the exact worst-case fraction [MATH] of gains obtained by the best price satisfies [MATH] as [MATH]. The worst-case buyer has two constant segments joined by an explicit nonexponential curve, approached through a vanishing atom whose value tends to infinity. The same constant is the exact guarantee of dominant-strategy mechanisms with individual rationality and strong budget balance in every realization. For two units with increasing submodular valuations, an explicit finite instance has ratio below [MATH], so multi-unit trade is strictly harder than single-unit trade. For any bounded ordered buyer pair we characterize the least common-price mass that guarantees a prescribed ratio against every ordered seller pair; a bound on this one-sided functional would determine the exact two-unit constant. Within an explicit family the unique minimum is [MATH], conjectured to be optimal.
tldr: The paper exactly determines the worst-case welfare guarantee of fixed-price bilateral trade, closing a gap in the mechanism design literature by characterizing the optimal posted price and worst-case buyer distribution.
motivation: Prior work from SODA 2016 through STOC 2023 and AAAI 2026 left a gap between known upper and lower bounds for the welfare guarantee of simple posted-price mechanisms in bilateral trade.
method: The authors formulate the worst-case guarantee as an optimization over buyer distributions and provide an explicit certificate of optimality via a change of variables that makes the gap a sum of nonnegative integrals, analogous to a linear-programming dual.
result: They prove the best posted price guarantees an explicit constant fraction of first-best welfare, identify the unique worst-case buyer shape, derive the exact tradeoff between gains from trade and initial seller welfare, and show that multi-unit trade is strictly harder than single-unit trade.
conclusion: This work resolves a long-standing open problem in fixed-price bilateral trade and provides a complete characterization of the worst-case welfare guarantee, with implications for dominant-strategy mechanisms and multi-unit settings.

title: Render Before Reading: Visual Rendering As A Prompt Injection Defense
authors: Jie Zhang, Andrei Baroian, Jan N. van Rijn, Avital Shafran, Florian Tram\`{e}r
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, where third-party adversarial content can hijack the model's behavior. In this paper, we study the role played by the adversarial data's input modality, and identify a systematic asymmetry: multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instruction when they appear as text than when the same instruction is delivered through a non-textual channel (e.g., as an image). We hypothesize that this modality gap arises from text-centric instruction tuning, which teaches models to obey textual instructions while treating other modalities mainly as content to parse or describe. We then demonstrate how this gap can be turned into a training-free defense, by rendering all untrusted payloads as typographic images (or audio) before they reach the model. Across ten models and two prompt injection benchmarks (DirectInject and AgentDojo) we show that our defense Pictionary consistently reduces attack success rates even against the strongest adaptive attacks and human red teamers, while largely preserving benign utility. We further show that benign fine-tuning on image-rendered instructions erodes the modality gap, tracing it to the text-centric instruction-tuning distribution.
tldr: This paper identifies a modality gap in multimodal LLMs where textual adversarial instructions are more effective than non-textual ones, and uses this gap to build a training-free prompt injection defense by rendering untrusted payloads as images or audio.
motivation: Large language models are vulnerable to prompt injection via third-party content, and the role of input modality in such attacks was underexplored.
method: The authors compare text-based versus image/audio-based adversarial instructions, hypothesize a text-centric instruction-tuning bias, and propose rendering all untrusted payloads as typographic images (or audio) before model ingestion.
result: Across ten models and two benchmarks, the defense reduces attack success rates against adaptive attacks and human red teamers while largely preserving benign utility; fine-tuning on image-rendered instructions erodes the modality gap.
conclusion: The modality asymmetry can be exploited as a practical, training-free defense against prompt injection, with the effect traced to text-centric instruction tuning.

title: Arrival-Time Incentive Compatibility In Random Order Online Bipartite Matching
authors: Varun Gupta Arghya Chakraborty
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we initiate the study of competitive algorithms with arrival-time incentive compatibility for random-order online bipartite matching in settings where the users care only about receiving service (matched vs. unmatched) and not which offline resource serves them, while the platform's objective is to maximize total matching reward. This captures applications such as ride-sharing where the users primarily care about being matched to a ride while the platform internalizes the cost of dispatching a distant driver; dispatching homogeneous service requests to heterogeneous servers (cloud/edge routing); and assigning customer requests to a pool of providers with different flexibility (e.g., English-only vs. bilingual agents). Our main question is: Motivated by the LP-based treatment of incentive compatibility in the classical secretary problem by Buchbinder et al., we impose a constraint that the ex ante probability of selection is equalized across all arrival positions. We answer our main question in the affirmative and propose the first constant-competitive algorithm for incentive compatible edge-weighted random-order online matching on complete bipartite graphs. The competitive ratio of our algorithm is parameterized by the imbalance factor [MATH] -- where [MATH] and [MATH] are the numbers of online and offline nodes, respectively, and [MATH] is a positive integer. In particular, we obtain a competitive guarantee of the form [MATH] where [MATH] and [MATH] as [MATH]. We also present algorithms with strictly improved competitive ratio of [MATH] for the binary-weighted case ([MATH]-[MATH] rewards).
tldr: The paper initiates the study of competitive algorithms with arrival-time incentive compatibility for random-order online bipartite matching, providing constant-competitive algorithms under an ex ante selection-probability equalization constraint.
motivation: Motivated by applications such as ride-sharing and cloud/edge routing where users care only about being matched while the platform maximizes reward, the authors address the lack of incentive compatibility in random-order online bipartite matching.
method: They impose an ex ante probability of selection equalized across arrival positions, inspired by LP-based incentive compatibility in the secretary problem, and design competitive algorithms for edge-weighted matching on complete bipartite graphs.
result: They give the first constant-competitive algorithm for incentive-compatible edge-weighted random-order online matching, with competitive ratio parameterized by an imbalance factor, and improved competitive ratios for binary-weighted cases.
conclusion: The work shows that incentive compatibility can be achieved with constant competitive guarantees in random-order online bipartite matching, opening a new direction for mechanism-aware online matching.

title: Nonreciprocal Chiral Automata
authors: Andrew A. Allocca, Armin Rahmani, Pouyan Ghaemi, Sriram Ganeshan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Odd pressure is a parity-odd transport coefficient that gives an isotropic pressure response to vorticity in compressible two-dimensional fluids. By asymmetrically coupling vortical and compressional modes, it provides a direct mechanism for a nonreciprocal hydrodynamic response reminiscent of several biological systems. Yet microscopic models realizing odd pressure as a transport coefficient are relatively scarce. Here, we construct one such model using a lattice-gas cellular automaton based on the Frisch-Hasslacher-Pomeau II model with rest particles and chiral collisions, whose Chapman-Enskog coarse-graining produces a nonzero odd pressure coefficient. The key ingredient is a local parity-breaking collision that weakly rotates moving particles in the presence of a rest particle. At hydrodynamic scales, this microscopic rule acts as an effective magnetic field, converting the model's bulk viscosity into odd pressure. More generally, we derive expressions relating Hall viscosity, odd pressure, and odd torque to their parity-even counterparts in our model.
tldr: This paper constructs a lattice-gas cellular automaton with chiral collisions to realize a nonzero odd pressure coefficient in two-dimensional fluids.
motivation: Odd pressure is a parity-odd transport coefficient that produces nonreciprocal hydrodynamic responses, but microscopic models realizing it are scarce.
method: The authors modify the Frisch-Hasslacher-Pomeau II lattice-gas cellular automaton by adding rest particles and a local parity-breaking collision rule, then use Chapman-Enskog coarse-graining to derive hydrodynamic transport coefficients.
result: The chiral collision rule yields a nonzero odd pressure coefficient, and the authors relate Hall viscosity, odd pressure, and odd torque to their parity-even counterparts.
conclusion: A simple local parity-breaking rule can generate odd pressure at hydrodynamic scales, providing a microscopic cellular-automaton model for nonreciprocal chiral fluids.

title: Dual-Anchor Acceleration Is Near-Optimal For Stochastic Monotone Root-Finding
authors: Nicolas Loizou Taeho Yoon
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Among distinct optimal acceleration mechanisms for deterministic monotone root-finding problems and fixed-point problems, dual-anchoring has recently been shown to admit a more robust direct stochastic extension than standard anchor acceleration. However, without additional strong monotonicity, the existing stochastic dual-anchoring guarantee has two limitations: first, it requires cocoercivity in expectation, and second, it attains only [MATH] oracle complexity, leaving a gap to the near-optimal [MATH] complexity achieved by other methods. In this work, we address both of these limitations by combining dual-anchoring with stochastic resolvent approximation and optimized variance control. For unbiased stochastic oracles with variance bounded by [MATH], where sample operators are monotone and uniformly [MATH]-Lipschitz, our algorithm finds a point with [MATH]-residual with a near-optimal oracle complexity of [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] is the initial distance to a solution. This result improves the best known oracle complexity in the noise-dominated regime under these samplewise assumptions, reducing the poly-logarithmic factor from cubic to quadratic.
tldr: This paper develops a dual-anchoring method with stochastic resolvent approximation and variance control that achieves near-optimal oracle complexity for stochastic monotone root-finding problems.
motivation: Existing stochastic dual-anchoring guarantees for monotone root-finding require cocoercivity in expectation and only reach suboptimal oracle complexity, leaving a gap to the near-optimal complexity attained by other methods.
method: The authors combine dual-anchoring with stochastic resolvent approximation and optimized variance control, analyzing unbiased stochastic monotone oracles with bounded variance and uniform Lipschitz sample operators.
result: The algorithm finds a point with the desired residual using near-optimal oracle complexity, improving the best known complexity in the noise-dominated regime by reducing the poly-logarithmic factor from cubic to quadratic.
conclusion: Dual-anchor acceleration is shown to be near-optimal for stochastic monotone root-finding, closing much of the gap to optimal complexity under weaker assumptions.

title: Beyond The Analytic Solution Manufacturing For Anisotropic Elliptic Equations
authors: Fabrice Deluzet, Valdimir Latocha, Fr\'ed\'eric Robert
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article is aimed at introducing a new procedure to define reference solutions to which the numerical approximations of anisotropic problems arising in plasma physics may be compared. In this context, the main issue is related to the construction of functions with no gradients along the vector field defining the anisotropy direction. The so-called solution manufacturing, implemented so far in the literature, only applies to frame- work where all the computations can be carried out analytically. In the present paper, we propose a new method in which this requirement is not mandatory. Indeed, via a Riemannian metric, we use a propagation of the boundary value by the flows related to the vector field defining the anisotropy direction. This permits to extend the application of the solution manufacturing to a broader range of contexts.
tldr: The paper introduces a Riemannian-metric-based method for manufacturing reference solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in plasma physics, extending beyond analytically solvable cases.
motivation: Existing manufactured solution techniques for anisotropic plasma problems are limited to frameworks where all computations can be done analytically, restricting their applicability to complex geometries or coefficients.
method: The authors use a Riemannian metric to propagate boundary values along the flows of the vector field defining the anisotropy direction, thereby constructing reference solutions without requiring analytical tractability.
result: The proposed procedure broadens the class of anisotropic elliptic problems for which manufactured solutions can be generated, enabling numerical validation in more general settings.
conclusion: This work provides a flexible new tool for verifying numerical approximations of anisotropic plasma physics models, though it is not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Equipotentials And Folds For Quasiregular Mandelbrot Sets
authors: Alastair N. Fletcher
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well-known that Douady and Hubbard proved that the Mandelbrot set is connected by constructing a uniformizing holomorphic map for its complement from the B\"ottcher coordinates. This strategy has a clear analogue in the setting of quasiregular Mandelbrot sets. In this paper, we show that the natural generalization of the Douady-Hubbard uniformizing map is quasiconformal in a neighbourhood of infinity, as well as, in fact, outside a certain neighbourhood of the quasiregular Mandelbrot set. On the other hand, we also show that this uniformizing map can reverse orientation at some parameters, which forces it to have folds and, in particular, prevents it from being injective. This feature cannot happen in the holomorphic setting. The connectivity of the quasiregular Mandelbrot sets therefore cannot be established along the Douady-Hubbard route, and remains open.
tldr: The paper studies the generalization of the Douady-Hubbard uniformizing map to quasiregular Mandelbrot sets, showing it is quasiconformal near infinity but can develop folds and fail injectivity, blocking that route to proving connectivity.
motivation: Douady and Hubbard proved the classical Mandelbrot set is connected by constructing a uniformizing holomorphic map from Bottcher coordinates; the author asks whether the analogous strategy works for quasiregular Mandelbrot sets.
method: The natural generalization of the Douady-Hubbard uniformizing map is analyzed using quasiconformal mapping theory, examining its behavior near infinity and outside a neighborhood of the quasiregular Mandelbrot set.
result: The map is shown to be quasiconformal in a neighborhood of infinity and outside a neighborhood of the set, but it can reverse orientation at some parameters, forcing folds and precluding injectivity.
conclusion: Orientation reversal is impossible in the holomorphic setting, so connectivity of quasiregular Mandelbrot sets cannot be established via the Douady-Hubbard route and remains open.

title: Ci-pinn: Causal Integral Physics-Informed Neural Network For Solving Evolution Equations
authors: Xiaodong Feng, Ziyu Sun, Tao Tang, Xiaoliang Wan, Tao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by incorporating governing physical laws into the training loss. For evolution equations, however, their conventional pointwise space--time representation does not explicitly encode temporal dependence, which can hinder accurate prediction. To mitigate this limitation, this work proposes a novel neural architecture termed a causal integral neural network (CinNet). The core module of CinNet is a Volterra-type causal integral term, which aggregates historical features to encode temporal dependence, thereby incorporating temporal causality at the architectural level rather than through training-level modifications as in many existing methods. Building on CinNet, we further develop a causal integral physics-informed neural network (CI-PINN) for solving evolution equations. Extensive numerical experiments on benchmark evolution equations demonstrate that the presented method outperforms various baseline PINN variants in terms of solution accuracy, with pronounced superiority under sparse-collocation scenarios. Additional empirical analyses show that CI-PINN exhibits low sensitivity to hyperparameter choices, while ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the proposed network components.
tldr: CI-PINN introduces a causal integral neural network with Volterra-type memory to better solve evolution PDEs by encoding temporal dependence directly into the architecture.
motivation: Standard physics-informed neural networks use pointwise space-time representations that do not explicitly capture temporal causality, which can degrade accuracy for evolution equations, especially with sparse collocation points.
method: The paper proposes CinNet, whose core module aggregates historical features via a Volterra-type causal integral term, and builds CI-PINN for solving evolution equations.
result: Numerical experiments on benchmark evolution equations show CI-PINN outperforms various baseline PINN variants in accuracy, with pronounced advantages in sparse-collocation scenarios and low hyperparameter sensitivity.
conclusion: The architectural incorporation of causal integral terms is an effective way to improve PINNs for evolution equations, and ablation studies validate the proposed components.

title: GenoTrace: Inheritable Watermarks For Genome Foundation Model Distillation
authors: Fengchen Liu Guang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a genome model retain a detectable record of the synthetic sequences used to train it? We study watermark inheritance through distillation with GenoTrace, a codon-aware extension of green-list watermarking. Two token-level factors modulate the teacher's generation bias using codon position and organism-specific codon usage. The resulting sequences train a smaller student, whose outputs are audited without an active watermark processor. In a three-seed GenomeOcean-500M-to-100M experiment, the joint configuration achieves a mean audit score of 17.88 and 94.5% detection at a fixed threshold. It retains 49.0% detection after key-aware token substitution, compared with 0% for the available single-seed plain-watermark comparator, and 47.0% after combined mechanism-targeted nucleotide edits. Additional experiments establish inherited signal across five organism-conditioned datasets and teacher-student size ratios up to 40. Component ablations and computational sequence-quality assays reveal distinct operating points for detection strength and coding coverage. GenoTrace provides a practical token-level construction and an empirical account of how genomic structure shapes inherited watermark signals. The findings concern shared-tokenizer distillation and the tested editing procedures, with calibration and biological utility treated as separate evaluation requirements.
tldr: GenoTrace introduces a codon-aware green-list watermarking method for genome foundation models that can be inherited by distilled student models.
motivation: The paper asks whether a genome model can retain a detectable record of synthetic sequences used in training, and studies watermark inheritance through distillation.
method: It extends green-list watermarking with codon position and organism-specific codon usage, then audits distilled student outputs without an active watermark processor.
result: In GenomeOcean-500M-to-100M experiments, the joint configuration achieves a mean audit score of 17.88 and 94.5% detection, retaining 49.0% detection after key-aware token substitution and 47.0% after targeted nucleotide edits.
conclusion: The work provides a practical token-level watermarking construction and empirical evidence for how genomic structure affects inherited watermark signals, with calibration and biological utility left as separate evaluation requirements.

title: Agentic Commerce Bench: Measuring Fraud Detection For Agents That Spend Money
authors: Debjyoti Paul Ankit Srivastava
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents now hold spend authority and settle payments without per-action human confirmation. The resulting loss is often not a security failure: a counterparty with the correct domain, the correct settlement address and a genuinely delivered service can charge more than it should, and no check keyed on identity will see it. We present three artefacts for measuring and reducing that loss. First, a taxonomy of agentic commerce fraud that separates five observation levels (agent reasoning, wire, settlement rail, counterparty, principal) from the request-level and history-level evidence available at each, and records which levels can observe which attacks. Second, Agentic Commerce Bench (ACB), a benchmark of twenty fraud classes generated from production aggregates, 1,647 catalogued service operations and 1,068 settlements, of which six involve a counterparty that is exactly who it claims to be. Third, gordonguard, an open-source detector stack and offline harness with which an operator can audit an agent configuration, replay hostile counterparties without an account, and run the same detectors inline. Calibrating to a stated false-positive budget on clean training traffic gives a 6.5% clean flag rate, replicated across three independent generations, and leaves eight of twenty classes no better than chance. On the four classes a reasoning layer can observe, a widely used agent security scanner run over its jailbreak-detection panel scores zero on all four, while correctly scoring 1.0 on a jailbreak supplied as a control. A measured median payment of $0.007 places a hard constraint on deployment: one human review costs 143 times the value of the payment it examines.
tldr: The paper introduces a taxonomy, benchmark (Agentic Commerce Bench), and open-source detector stack (gordonguard) for measuring and mitigating fraud in AI-agent payment transactions.
motivation: AI agents increasingly hold spend authority and settle payments without per-action human confirmation, enabling a class of loss that is not a conventional security failure and cannot be caught by identity-keyed checks.
method: The authors build a five-level observation taxonomy (agent reasoning, wire, settlement rail, counterparty, principal), a benchmark of twenty fraud classes drawn from production aggregates (1,647 service operations, 1,068 settlements), and an offline harness for auditing agent configurations and replaying hostile counterparties.
result: Calibration to a stated false-positive budget yields a 6.5% clean flag rate replicated across three generations, while eight of twenty fraud classes remain no better than chance; a widely used agent security scanner scores zero on all four reasoning-layer-observable classes (but 1.0 on a jailbreak control), and a $0.007 median payment means one human review costs 143x the payment value.
conclusion: Agentic commerce fraud requires dedicated multi-level measurement and detection infrastructure, and current generic security scanners are inadequate; economic constraints severely limit human-in-the-loop mitigation.

title: Dual-Fit Imperative In Security Leadership: A Grounded Theory Investigation Of Ciso Role Enactment In Modern Organisations
authors: Mazino Benson Onibere
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) has emerged as a strategically prominent executive role, confronting an adversarial environment, irreconcilable accountability tensions between security and business enablement, and a prevention paradox in which success remains invisible to resource allocators. Scholarly understanding of how the role operates across organisational contexts remains virtually absent, leaving practice without empirical foundation. This thesis asks: how is the CISO role enacted across different organisational contexts in modern organisations? The study employs constructivist grounded theory with an abductive reasoning framework and the Gioia method, drawing on twenty interviews with Australian security executives. The CISO role is not a stable configuration of responsibilities applied uniformly, but a continuously negotiated achievement. Effectiveness emerges from dual-fit maintenance: alignment between the leader and the internal organisational context (CISO-Organisation Fit) and the external environment (CISO-Environment Fit). These requirements transform across three maturity phases, Establishment, Maturation, and Strategic, with action-oriented, stewardship-oriented, and vision-oriented leaders generating effectiveness in each; effectiveness in one phase can undermine it in another. Political capital is the mechanism through which leaders navigate these shifting demands. These patterns are synthesised in the Security Leadership Contingency Model (SLCM), the thesis's primary theoretical contribution. Instruments developed from the model translate these insights into guidance for leadership selection and succession planning. The SLCM extends person-organisation fit, person-environment fit, and contingency theory to security leadership, advancing understanding of executive effectiveness under accountability tensions and evolving contextual demands.
tldr: A grounded theory study of how Chief Information Security Officers enact their role across organisational contexts, proposing the Security Leadership Contingency Model based on 20 interviews with Australian security executives.
motivation: The CISO role has become strategically prominent yet scholarly understanding of how it operates across organisations is virtually absent, leaving practice without empirical foundation.
method: Constructivist grounded theory with an abductive reasoning framework and the Gioia method, drawing on twenty interviews with Australian security executives.
result: CISO effectiveness emerges from 'dual-fit maintenance' (CISO-Organisation Fit and CISO-Environment Fit) that shifts across Establishment, Maturation, and Strategic maturity phases, with political capital as the mediating mechanism; these patterns are synthesised into the Security Leadership Contingency Model.
conclusion: The SLCM extends person-organisation fit, person-environment fit, and contingency theory to security leadership, yielding instruments for leadership selection and succession planning.

title: Tee Anchor: Cross-TEE Organizational Endorsement For Mitigating Tee Physical Attacks
authors: Ao Sakurai
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2025, practical physical-access attacks against TEEs, such as TEE.fail and Battering RAM, were disclosed, posing a serious threat to current TEEs. The more strictly the target machine is guarded, the harder such attacks are to mount. Residing under trusted management has therefore emerged as a new security requirement. Yet existing attestation cannot prove a machine's organizational affiliation. This leaves room for an attacker to pass off a physically accessible machine under their control as one operated in a legitimate environment. We propose TEE Anchor, a mechanism that mitigates physical attacks by proving which organization manages a machine. TEE Anchor is a lightweight, X.509-based design that needs no additional root of trust such as a (v)TPM. The organization issues a certificate over the Chip ID, a unique per-CPU identifier, forming its own PKI. A Verifier then proves affiliation by matching the Chip ID in the attestation evidence against that certificate. This outperforms (v)TPM-based prior work in operational cost and deployability, applies across major TEEs without vendor lock-in, and lets any organization assert affiliation independently of TEE vendors. We implemented a prototype and confirmed that all operations, including provisioning and verification, complete within a few milliseconds.
tldr: TEE Anchor is a lightweight X.509-based mechanism that proves which organization manages a machine by certifying the CPU's unique Chip ID, thereby mitigating physical-access attacks on trusted execution environments.
motivation: Recent physical-access attacks (TEE.fail, Battering RAM) show that strict physical guarding of machines is a real security requirement, but existing attestation cannot prove a machine's organizational affiliation, letting attackers pass off physically accessible machines as legitimately operated ones.
method: The organization issues an X.509 certificate over the platform's Chip ID, forming its own PKI without needing an additional root of trust such as a (v)TPM; a verifier matches the Chip ID in the attestation evidence against that certificate to prove affiliation.
result: A prototype implementation shows all operations, including provisioning and verification, complete within a few milliseconds, and the design outperforms (v)TPM-based prior work in operational cost and deployability while remaining vendor-agnostic across major TEEs.
conclusion: Cross-TEE organizational endorsement via Chip ID certificates offers a cheap, deployable way to strengthen attestation against physical attacks, though it is a classical systems-security contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-platform content.

title: Pseudo-solutions Of Polynomial Systems And The Lower Bound Problem For $\mbox{AC}^0[p]$-Frege Systems
authors: Jana Kraj\'i\vcek
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem to establish a lower bound for [MATH]-Frege refutations of a system of polynomial equations over [MATH] was in K. (2024) reduced to the existence of a pseudo-solution (a notion defined there) for the system. Here we reduce this further, for the system expressing the negation of the PHP, to a property of search trees querying values of linear maps on the vector space of low degree polynomials over [MATH].
tldr: This paper reduces the lower bound problem for AC^0[p]-Frege refutations of polynomial systems to a property of search trees querying linear maps on low-degree polynomials.
motivation: Establishing lower bounds for AC^0[p]-Frege systems is a central open problem in proof complexity, with connections to circuit complexity.
method: The author builds on a prior reduction to pseudo-solutions and further reduces the problem, for the system expressing the negation of the PHP, to a combinatorial property of search trees over vector spaces of low-degree polynomials.
result: The reduction connects proof complexity lower bounds to search tree properties, potentially offering a new combinatorial approach to the lower bound problem.
conclusion: This is a purely classical complexity result that does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
