title: PrivacySkills: How Privacy Guidance Shapes Source Selection In Llm Agents
authors: Lucas Biechy, C\'edric Eichler, H\'eber H. Arcolezi, Nicolas Anciaux
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While prior work has documented privacy failures in LLM agents, it remains unclear how the presentation of privacy guidance influences their choice of information sources. We introduce PrivacySkills, a controlled framework for evaluating how agents choose among acquisition pathways that provide the same task-relevant value: consulting publicly available personal information, accessing confidential sources, or interacting with the user. The evaluation framework comprises 55 synthetic tasks spanning 11 categories of personal information, with 169 associated skills that describe the available acquisition pathways. We consider privacy guidance through system-level instructions, skill-level metadata labels, or both. Separately, we vary user availability and urgency framing. With users available and no privacy guidance, agents access confidential sources in 30% of valid runs on average across five open-weight models, despite sufficient alternatives. This rate increases to 45% when users are unavailable, whereas urgency framing has no detectable effect. System-level privacy instructions alone have limited effects on confidential access, while skill-level intrusiveness labels produce a modest reduction (24% on average), but combining the two roughly halves confidential access. Our findings motivate incorporating privacy annotations into skill specifications and evaluating their effectiveness alongside system-level instructions.
tldr: PrivacySkills is a controlled evaluation framework showing how different forms of privacy guidance (system-level instructions vs. skill-level metadata labels) shape LLM agents' choice among public, confidential, and user-interaction information sources.
motivation: Prior work has documented privacy failures in LLM agents, but it is unclear how the presentation of privacy guidance influences which information acquisition pathways agents choose when alternatives of equal task value exist.
method: The authors build 55 synthetic tasks across 11 categories of personal information with 169 associated skills describing acquisition pathways, then vary privacy guidance (system instructions, skill-level labels, or both), user availability, and urgency framing across five open-weight models.
result: Without privacy guidance, agents accessed confidential sources in ~30% of valid runs when users were available, rising to 45% when users were unavailable; system-level instructions alone had limited effect, skill-level labels modestly reduced access (24%), and combining both roughly halved confidential access.
conclusion: The findings motivate embedding privacy annotations directly into skill specifications and evaluating their effectiveness jointly with system-level instructions.

title: DecoyTrace: Toxic Decoys For Active Defense In Decentralized Federated Learning
authors: Pedro Beltr\'an-L\'opez, Enrique Tom\'as Mart\'inez Beltr\'an, Pantaleone Nespoli, Manuel Gil P\'erez, Alberto Huertas Celdr\'an
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) eliminates the central aggregation server, reducing the single point of observation that traditional defenses against attacks rely on. As a result, peer-to-peer networks become exposed to malicious updates containing backdoors or semantic poisoning, since such updates can remain close to benign ones in the parameter space while behaving very differently. This may evade defenses based on passive parameter inspection. However, existing deception-based defenses have mainly been designed for centralized FL and do not jointly address local observation, poisoning propagation, source attribution, and containment in strictly serverless DFL. To address these limitations, this paper presents DecoyTrace, a proactive cyber deception-based defense for strictly serverless DFL environments. DecoyTrace deploys a mobile DecoyNode that generates decoy challenges using chaotic maps, disseminates a dual model (clean vs. decoy) based on neighbor trust, and evaluates them using three-state semantic metrics. Upon confirmation, a distributed protocol isolates the source and performs a model reset or recovery to preserve training progress. Evaluated across sixty configurations on the NEBULA platform (five datasets, three topologies, and four attack/defense scenarios), DecoyTrace systematically restores lost utility. The F1-score remains within 0.03 of the baseline on MNIST/FashionMNIST (mitigating drops of up to 0.37), matches or exceeds the baseline on EMNIST and CIFAR-100, and remains between 0.05 and 0.10 below the baseline on CIFAR-10, the most visually complex convolutional scenario evaluated. Furthermore, containment reduces CPU and network usage by up to two-thirds. These results demonstrate the feasibility of unifying deception, identification, and containment in DFL, while also identifying its limitations in complex tasks and multi-attractor threat models.
tldr: DecoyTrace is a proactive cyber-deception defense for strictly serverless decentralized federated learning that unifies decoy-based detection, source attribution, and containment of poisoning/backdoor attacks.
motivation: Decentralized federated learning removes the central aggregator, eliminating the single observation point on which most defenses rely, leaving peer-to-peer networks exposed to stealthy malicious updates that evade passive parameter inspection.
method: A mobile DecoyNode issues chaotic-map-generated decoy challenges, disseminates a dual clean/decoy model based on neighbor trust, and evaluates updates via three-state semantic metrics; upon confirmation a distributed protocol isolates the source and triggers model reset or recovery.
result: Across sixty configurations on the NEBULA platform (five datasets, three topologies, four scenarios), F1 stays within 0.03 of baseline on MNIST/FashionMNIST (mitigating drops up to 0.37), matches or exceeds baseline on EMNIST and CIFAR-100, and trails by 0.05–0.10 on CIFAR-10, with containment cutting CPU and network usage by up to two-thirds.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the feasibility of unifying deception, identification, and containment in serverless DFL, while exposing limitations in visually complex tasks and multi-attractor threat models.

title: CounterSteer: Suppressing Indirect Prompt Injection With Activation Steering
authors: Mark Russinovich
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indirect prompt injection makes an LLM agent treat untrusted retrieved text as instructions. We present CounterSteer, an inference-time defense that suppresses this behavior inside the model. Per model, a five-step recipe fits a residual-stream direction from paired episodes differing only in whether an embedded instruction is followed, and retains it only if it passes pre-specified causal and capability gates. At deployment, the direction is subtracted from every tool-result token during prefill. The edit is always on--there is no detection decision to evade--and requires no fine-tuning, auxiliary model, or added tokens, only white-box serving and tool-result span boundaries. Across five open-weights models (8B-106B, five vendor lineages), held-out attack success falls from 0.21-1.00 undefended to 0.00-0.17 defended, and AgentDojo compromise rate from 0.10-0.49 to 0.006-0.079, at 93-100% typography-normalized benign utility, with larger task-dependent costs when reasoning over steered content. A benchmark-level adaptive attacker reaching 0.67-0.73 undefended is held to roughly a quarter of that on the two most deeply evaluated models. Among the defenses we measured on capable models, those achieving lower compromise rates either lost 22-89% of benign utility or fine-tuned the served weights. White-box gradient attacks through the deployed vector compromise at most 2 of 52 episodes, and none of 2,052 replayed human red-team attacks succeeds. CounterSteer largely neutralizes instructional takeover: a black-box framing search cracks 3 of 18 development samples. Parameter manipulation--attacker-chosen arguments in otherwise legitimate calls--is only partially resisted (13 of 18); the decision becomes linearly readable at argument emission but not at the examined pre-generation sites, and is not removed by the tested prefill- or decode-time steering, motivating argument-provenance controls.
tldr: CounterSteer is an inference-time activation-steering defense that subtracts a fitted residual-stream direction from tool-result tokens to suppress indirect prompt injection in LLM agents.
motivation: Indirect prompt injection causes LLM agents to treat untrusted retrieved text as instructions, and existing defenses either lose benign utility or require fine-tuning of served weights.
method: For each model, a five-step recipe fits a residual-stream direction from paired episodes that differ only in whether an embedded instruction was followed, validates it against causal and capability gates, and subtracts it from every tool-result token during prefill without detection, fine-tuning, or extra tokens.
result: Across five open-weights models (8B–106B), held-out attack success drops from 0.21–1.00 to 0.00–0.17 and AgentDojo compromise rate from 0.10–0.49 to 0.006–0.079, at 93–100% benign utility, though adaptive black-box and parameter-manipulation attacks are only partially resisted.
conclusion: CounterSteer largely neutralizes instructional takeover in LLM agents with minimal utility loss, but parametric manipulation of legitimate tool arguments remains an open problem motivating argument-provenance controls.

title: Hybrid Work And The Restructuring Of Urban Mobility In U.s. Cities
authors: Marta C. Gonz\'alez Baoqi Eileen Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entering the post-pandemic era, cities navigate a new normal shaped by hybrid work and space-time flexibility, but existing evidence is spatially scattered and temporally limited. Here we develop an analytical approach that examines this reorganization through three dimensions: remote work adoption via sector composition, daily travel behavior via trip-level metrics, and functional urban form via mobility-derived measures. To capture the interplay of urban dynamics, we synthesize three complementary spatial metrics. In particular, coupling overall trip centrality with work-trip concentration differentiates whether employment and daily activity organize around the same centers. Applied to population-scale data across 15 U.S. metropolitan areas spanning 2019-2024, our approach shows that daily car travel increased despite elevated remote work, a pattern consistent across cities with distinct spatial structures. Decomposition and regression identify trip frequency as the primary contributor to VKT growth, moderated by compact urban form and concentrated employment. The approach provides a replicable framework for comparative study of post-pandemic urban mobility.
tldr: The paper analyzes post-pandemic urban mobility restructuring in U.S. cities under hybrid work, showing increased car travel despite elevated remote work.
motivation: Post-pandemic hybrid work has reshaped urban travel and spatial organization, but evidence remains spatially scattered and temporally limited.
method: The authors synthesize three complementary spatial metrics and apply decomposition and regression to population-scale mobility data from 15 U.S. metropolitan areas spanning 2019-2024.
result: Daily car travel increased across cities despite more remote work, with trip frequency as the primary contributor to VKT growth, moderated by compact urban form and concentrated employment.
conclusion: The framework offers a replicable approach for comparative study of post-pandemic urban mobility and highlights the complex relationship between remote work and travel demand.

title: A Hypotenuse-Angle Axiomatization Of The Hilbert Plane
authors: Roberto Volpe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, in [MATH] --- [MATH], the Hilbert plane, deprived of the Side-Angle-Side axiom --- a hypotenuse-angle criterion for right triangles, together with the existence of a perpendicular from an external point to a line and a ray correspondence principle governing the ordering of angles, suffices to reconstruct SAS in full --- and hence, as standard consequences, SSS and SAA as well. This offers a more elementary alternative to Hilbert's own choice of SAS as an axiom, confined throughout to right triangles and provable without any continuity assumption. Several recent papers have proposed related alternatives on comparable grounds; we compare our approach to theirs in the concluding remarks. The result builds on, and is best read alongside, two earlier papers of ours on related reconstructions of SAS .
tldr: The paper provides a hypotenuse-angle axiomatization of the Hilbert plane, reconstructing the Side-Angle-Side axiom without continuity assumptions.
motivation: The work aims to offer a more elementary alternative to Hilbert's choice of SAS as an axiom by using a right-triangle criterion and related principles.
method: The authors replace the SAS axiom with a hypotenuse-angle criterion, the existence of perpendiculars from external points, and a ray correspondence principle, then derive SAS and standard consequences.
result: They show that SAS, SSS, and SAA can be reconstructed from the alternative axioms, confined to right triangles and provable without continuity assumptions.
conclusion: This provides a foundational geometry result alternative to Hilbert's axiomatization, with comparisons to recent related proposals in the concluding remarks.

title: On Talagrand Type
authors: Nika Areshidze
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Rademacher type [MATH] coincides with Talagrand type [MATH] for every [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that Rademacher type and Talagrand type coincide for every p.
motivation: To clarify the relationship between two notions of type that appear in the geometry of Banach spaces and probabilistic inequalities.
method: A mathematical proof in functional analysis and probability theory, establishing an equivalence between the two type parameters.
result: For every p, Rademacher type p equals Talagrand type p.
conclusion: This advances pure mathematics but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantitative Dynamics Of Complex H\'enon Maps
authors: Henry de Th\'elin, Tien-Cuong Dinh, Lucas Kaufmann
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a H\'enon map of [MATH]. We provide quantitative versions of several results involving dynamical objects associated to [MATH]. Our results can be interpreted as a quantitative version of Pesin theory with geometric control. As an application we show that the perdiodic points of period [MATH] of [MATH] equidistribute towards its equilibrium measure exponentially fast as [MATH] tends to infinity.
tldr: The paper gives quantitative versions of dynamical results for complex Hénon maps, including exponential equidistribution of periodic points toward the equilibrium measure.
motivation: The authors aim to provide quantitative refinements of Pesin theory with geometric control for complex Hénon maps.
method: They use tools from complex dynamics, pluripotential theory, and geometric control to quantify dynamical objects associated with the map.
result: Periodic points of period n equidistribute exponentially fast toward the equilibrium measure as n tends to infinity.
conclusion: The work advances the quantitative understanding of complex Hénon map dynamics and equidistribution phenomena.

title: On The Value Function For A Class Of Set Motion Problems
authors: Alberto Bressan, Maria Teresa Chiri, Elsa M. Marchini
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper considers a class of optimal set motion problems, where the control determines the velocity of boundary points in the normal direction. Results and counterexamples are given, on the continuous dependence of the minimum cost from the initial configuration. The last sections of the paper study the slicing cost of bounded open sets. For strongly Lipschitz domains, it is proved that the slicing cost varies continuously w.r.t. the Hausdorff distance of the boundaries. We conjecture that the slicing cost for a disc is maximal among all sets with the same area.
tldr: The paper studies optimal set motion problems where boundary velocities are controlled, establishing continuity of minimum cost and analyzing slicing cost for bounded open sets.
motivation: The authors aim to understand continuous dependence of optimal costs on initial configurations and properties of slicing costs for sets under Hausdorff perturbations.
method: They formulate a class of optimal control problems for set motions, prove results and provide counterexamples, and analyze slicing cost for strongly Lipschitz domains.
result: They show continuity of minimum cost and slicing cost with respect to Hausdorff distance, and conjecture that the slicing cost for a disc is maximal among sets of equal area.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of set motion and geometric optimal control, but has no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Slicing Problems
authors: Alberto Bressan, Maria Teresa Chiri, Elsa M. Marchini
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a bounded open set [MATH], we consider the problem of slicing this set by a family of curves, whose average length is as small as possible. The first sections of the paper prove the existence of an optimal slicing and establish a connection with the problem of eradicating an invasive biological species from an island, considered in . Namely, an optimal slicing can be obtained as a limit of minimum time eradication strategies. The second part of the paper derives various necessary conditions for optimality, describing the behavior of an optimal slicing strategy in the interior of [MATH] and near the boundary [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies the geometric/optimal-control problem of slicing a bounded open set by a family of curves minimizing average length, connecting it to minimum-time strategies for eradicating an invasive species on an island.
motivation: The authors seek to characterize optimal ways to partition a planar domain by curves of minimal average length, motivated by an application to containment and eradication of an invasive biological population.
method: They prove existence of an optimal slicing via variational/optimal-control arguments and show it arises as a limit of minimum-time eradication strategies, then derive necessary optimality conditions both in the interior and near the boundary.
result: Existence of an optimal slicing is established, along with a link to time-optimal eradication, and a set of necessary conditions describing the local behavior of an optimal slicing strategy.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for optimal slicing problems and clarifies their relation to eradication strategies, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Feasibility Correction In Linear Programs
authors: Pedro Abdalla, Roman Vershynin, Guangyi Zou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study feasibility correction for linear programs. Suppose an initial point satisfies most of the constraints. Can it be moved into the feasible region without changing the objective value? Our main deterministic result says that this is possible if the constraint matrix satisfies a restricted isometry property (RIP). We apply the correction theorem to obtain lower bounds for random linear programs with finite-moment or sub-Weibull entries. We complement these with matching-order upper bounds under a uniform [MATH]th-moment bound for some [MATH] and a delocalization condition on the objective direction. As an application of our techniques, we also derive lower bounds for the Gaussian width of feasible regions under RIP assumptions.
tldr: The paper studies feasibility correction in linear programs, showing that a point satisfying most constraints can be moved into the feasible region without changing the objective under a restricted isometry property (RIP), with applications to random linear programs and Gaussian width bounds.
motivation: Feasibility correction is a fundamental problem in linear programming and optimization, with connections to robustness and random matrix theory. The authors aim to understand when an almost-feasible point can be corrected without worsening the objective.
method: They prove a deterministic correction theorem assuming the constraint matrix satisfies RIP, then apply it to random linear programs with finite-moment or sub-Weibull entries, and derive matching upper bounds under a uniform moment condition and a delocalization assumption.
result: The main result gives conditions under which feasibility correction is possible with no objective change, yielding lower bounds for random LPs and Gaussian width of feasible regions under RIP.
conclusion: The work provides new theoretical tools for linear programming and random matrix theory, but it is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Algebraic Vector Fields On $s^2$ Are $2$-generated
authors: Xudong Chen Yiyang Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit two vector fields on [MATH], which generate the entire Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields. Compositions of the flows associated with these two vector fields enable us to approximate every diffeomorphism of [MATH] isotopic to the identity in the [MATH]-sense for any [MATH].
tldr: The paper shows that two algebraic vector fields on the 2-sphere generate the entire Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields and can approximate every identity-isotopic diffeomorphism.
motivation: The work studies generating sets for Lie algebras of algebraic vector fields and the controllability/approximation of diffeomorphisms via flow compositions.
method: It constructs two explicit algebraic vector fields and uses their associated flows to generate the full Lie algebra and approximate diffeomorphisms in a suitable sense.
result: Two vector fields are sufficient to generate the entire Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields on S^2, and their flow compositions approximate every diffeomorphism isotopic to the identity.
conclusion: The algebraic vector fields on S^2 admit a 2-generator presentation, with consequences for approximating diffeomorphisms via iterated flows.

title: Residual Feedback For Transformed-State Equilibrium Seeking Via General Variational Inequalities
authors: Afrooz Jalilzadeh Griffin Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by networked systems in which equilibrium conditions apply to a regulated state rather than directly to the decision variable, we study transformed-state general variational inequalities. Using a projection-residual reformulation, we develop residual feedback methods that operate in the decision space without inverting the state mapping [MATH]. For a one-step method, we establish an [MATH] best-iterate residual rate under solution-restricted cocoercivity and linear convergence under solution-restricted strong monotonicity and residual Lipschitz continuity. We also obtain an [MATH] best-iterate residual rate for a predictor-corrector method applied to the induced GVI residual under monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity. The assumptions are imposed directly on the computable residual and are illustrated by affine network and rank-deficient examples. Finally, we extend the residual framework to generalized quasi-variational inequalities with decision-dependent feasible sets.
tldr: The paper develops residual feedback methods for transformed-state equilibrium seeking in general variational inequalities.
motivation: Motivated by networked systems where equilibrium conditions apply to a regulated state rather than directly to the decision variable.
method: Using a projection-residual reformulation, the authors propose one-step and predictor-corrector residual feedback methods that operate in the decision space without inverting the state mapping.
result: They establish best-iterate residual rates and linear convergence under solution-restricted cocoercivity, strong monotonicity, and residual Lipschitz continuity, and extend the framework to generalized quasi-variational inequalities.
conclusion: The assumptions are imposed directly on the computable residual and are illustrated with affine network and rank-deficient examples.

title: Koopman Observability Of Nonlinear Systems And Data-Driven Koopman--Luenberger Observer
authors: Wentao Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While nonlinear systems can be generally described as infinite-dimensional linear systems via their Koopman semigroups, the direct synthesis of state observers on the premise of learned Koopman operator models, in an analogous manner to finite-dimensional linear systems, remains an open problem. In this paper, the concepts of Koopman observability (exact and approximate), Koopman detectability (exponential and strong), and Koopman--Luenberger observer of nonlinear systems are provided. By defining the Koopman semigroup on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), the conditions for Koopman exponential detectability are established, which involves solving an operator Lyapunov inequality that only implicitly involves the the infinitesimal generator of the Koopman semigroup. Through the use of a finite-horizon Yosida approximation of the Koopman generator and an empirical sampling operator, the data-driven solution of the observer gain can be reduced to a finite-dimensional subspace specified by the sample and hence fulfilled by convex semidefinite programming. The state observation error is guaranteed to be bounded in mean squares, under closed-loop dissipation conditions on the sampling operator and its empirical operator.
tldr: Introduces Koopman observability, detectability, and a data-driven Koopman-Luenberger observer for nonlinear systems using RKHS and convex optimization.
motivation: While nonlinear systems can be represented as infinite-dimensional linear systems via Koopman semigroups, directly synthesizing state observers from learned Koopman operator models remains an open problem.
method: Defines the Koopman semigroup on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), establishes conditions for Koopman exponential detectability via an operator Lyapunov inequality, and uses a finite-horizon Yosida approximation with an empirical sampling operator to reduce observer gain design to convex semidefinite programming.
result: The state observation error is guaranteed to be bounded in mean squares under closed-loop dissipation conditions on the sampling operator and its empirical counterpart.
conclusion: The framework enables data-driven observer design for nonlinear systems through a convex optimization formulation analogous to finite-dimensional linear system observer synthesis.

title: IC-rigidity For Abelian Actions
authors: Adam Kanigowski, Kosma Kasprzak, Miriam Lorenzo-Laguno
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a group acting continuously on a compact metric space [MATH]. This naturally induces an action of [MATH] on the space [MATH] of nonempty compact subsets of [MATH]. In [KS26], Kra and Schmieding define a system [MATH] to be IC-rigid if the union of the supports of the [MATH]-invariant Borel probability measures on [MATH] is as small as possible. They leave open the question of existence of IC-rigid abelian systems. We show the existence of IC-rigid actions for three classes of abelian groups: mixing rank-one [MATH]-actions, horocycle flows, and certain mixing actions on a Cantor space of [MATH], where [MATH] is any sequence of nontrivial finite abelian groups. In the course of proving these results, we introduce the notion of weakly asymptotic pairs and establish its close connection to topological minimal self-joinings.
tldr: The paper proves the existence of IC-rigid abelian group actions for several classes of dynamical systems, including mixing rank-one actions, horocycle flows, and certain Cantor-space actions.
motivation: Kra and Schmieding defined IC-rigidity for topological dynamical systems and left open the existence question for abelian actions.
method: The authors introduce weakly asymptotic pairs and establish their connection to topological minimal self-joinings, then use these tools to construct and analyze IC-rigid abelian actions.
result: They show that mixing rank-one Z-actions, horocycle flows, and certain mixing actions on Cantor spaces with finite abelian group sequences are IC-rigid.
conclusion: This answers the open question by exhibiting IC-rigid abelian systems across three classes of examples and links IC-rigidity to weakly asymptotic pairs and topological minimal self-joinings.

title: A Unified Structure-preserving Framework For Geometric Flows With Coupled Orientation And Curvature Dependence
authors: Yulin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a structure-preserving parametric finite element framework for geometric flows whose energy density couples the unit normal and the curvature. This class includes bending energies with orientation-dependent rigidity or spontaneous curvature. A common fully discrete formulation treats closed curves in two dimensions and closed surfaces in three dimensions, and accommodates the [MATH] flow, curve or surface diffusion, and the area- or volume-constrained [MATH] flow. The formulation couples the geometric and curvature updates so that their contributions satisfy a discrete energy inequality. It uses continuous piecewise linear elements, a surface energy matrix, and a mass-lumped projection of the curvature derivative of the density. For positive densities satisfying a directional condition and convexity in curvature, we prove energy dissipation without a time-step restriction. The diffusion and constrained flows also preserve the enclosed area or volume exactly. The analysis allows non-even anisotropies and nonseparable dependence on orientation and curvature. Numerical experiments exhibit approximately second-order convergence in the manifold distance and confirm the discrete structural properties. Shape relaxation under an anisotropic Helfrich-type energy illustrates the use of the framework for coupled directional and bending effects.
tldr: The paper develops a structure-preserving parametric finite element framework for geometric flows with energy densities coupling orientation and curvature.
motivation: Many geometric flows involve anisotropic bending energies where the energy density depends jointly on the unit normal and curvature, and existing numerical methods often lack provable discrete energy dissipation or exact area/volume preservation.
method: The authors propose a fully discrete finite element formulation using continuous piecewise linear elements, a surface energy matrix, and a mass-lumped projection of the curvature derivative, treating closed curves in 2D and surfaces in 3D for several flows including Willmore flow, diffusion, and constrained flows.
result: They prove discrete energy dissipation without time-step restrictions under positive density and curvature convexity conditions, show exact area or volume preservation for diffusion and constrained flows, and numerically observe approximately second-order convergence.
conclusion: The framework unifies and extends structure-preserving numerical methods for geometric flows with coupled orientation and curvature dependence, as illustrated by anisotropic Helfrich-type shape relaxation.

title: Conditional-Coverage Contributor Selection For Regional Digital Twins Under Mobility
authors: Tao Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regional digital twins (DTs) under mobility must coordinate contributor admission over congested broadcast networks without fixed infrastructure. Per-sender redundancy mitigation cannot make this set-level decision because only the host has a region-wide coverage map. Treating regional state as a public good, this letter develops a host-coordinated protocol admitting contributors whose timely, non-redundant coverage gain exceeds a congestion price within a cycle deadline. A 13-byte beacon digest enables pre-transmission scoring. Standards-based simulation shows the protocol reduces the timely actionable coverage deficit from 5.6\% to 1.4\% at load comparable to ETSI redundancy mitigation and by 26\% versus random admission at matched tight-budget load.
tldr: A host-coordinated protocol selects contributors for regional digital twins by scoring their timely non-redundant coverage gain against a congestion price, using a compact beacon digest.
motivation: Regional digital twins under mobility require efficient contributor admission over congested broadcast networks without fixed infrastructure, and per-sender redundancy mitigation cannot solve the set-level coverage problem.
method: The paper develops a host-coordinated admission protocol that treats regional state as a public good, computes pre-transmission coverage gain scores from a 13-byte beacon digest, and enforces a cycle deadline.
result: Standards-based simulations show the protocol reduces the timely actionable coverage deficit from 5.6% to 1.4% at load comparable to ETSI redundancy mitigation and by 26% versus random admission under tight-budget load.
conclusion: The proposed conditional-coverage contributor selection improves coverage efficiency for regional digital twins under mobility, offering a practical admission control mechanism for infrastructure-less broadcast environments.

title: Structure-preserving Upwind Lagrange Multiplier Schemes For Solid-state Dewetting With A Logarithmic Flory--Huggins Potential
authors: Qiong-Ao Huang, Ying-Wei Wang, Cheng Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-field simulations of solid-state dewetting based on polynomial potentials may exhibit spurious bulk-diffusion coarsening, inconsistent with the surface-diffusion-dominated physics. To address this issue, we formulate a degenerate Cahn--Hilliard model with the logarithmic Flory--Huggins potential and dynamic contact line boundary conditions for the film--substrate--vapor triple junction. The logarithmic barrier confines the phase variable to its physical range and suppresses spurious coarsening at the continuum level. We develop a fully discrete, structure-preserving scheme that combines a Lagrange multiplier approach with an upwind finite-volume discretization and rigorously guarantees pointwise boundedness, mass conservation, and energy dissipation without artificial cut-offs or projections. A dimensional-splitting strategy further reduces computational cost while preserving these properties in each one-dimensional sweep. We also derive an explicit estimate of the equilibrium radius contraction caused by spontaneous film shrinking, showing that the logarithmic potential produces weaker spurious shrinkage than the polynomial potential. Numerical experiments confirm the analysis and demonstrate that, for small temperature parameters, the proposed scheme suppresses spurious coarsening and pinch-off while accurately reproducing surface-diffusion-dominated dynamics and relaxation toward equilibrium island structures.
tldr: This paper develops a structure-preserving numerical scheme for a degenerate Cahn--Hilliard model of solid-state dewetting using a logarithmic Flory--Huggins potential.
motivation: Polynomial potentials in phase-field simulations of solid-state dewetting can cause spurious bulk-diffusion coarsening that conflicts with surface-diffusion-dominated physics.
method: The authors formulate a degenerate Cahn--Hilliard model with dynamic contact line boundary conditions and propose a fully discrete scheme combining a Lagrange multiplier approach and upwind finite-volume discretization, with dimensional splitting for efficiency.
result: The scheme rigorously preserves pointwise boundedness, mass conservation, and energy dissipation, and numerical experiments show suppressed spurious coarsening and pinch-off while accurately reproducing surface-diffusion dynamics.
conclusion: The logarithmic Flory--Huggins potential yields weaker spurious shrinkage than polynomial potentials, and the proposed scheme provides a reliable structure-preserving tool for simulating solid-state dewetting.

title: The Critical Value For The Beurling-Type Theorem In Weighted Bergman Spaces
authors: Zhaopeng Lin, Shibo Xu, Tao Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every [MATH] we construct a finite set [MATH] such that the zero-based invariant subspace [MATH] fails the wandering subspace property. Consequently, the Beurling-type theorem holds on the weighted Bergman space [MATH] if and only if [MATH], confirming a conjecture of Shimorin. As a further application, we extend the prescribed-curvature construction of Hedenmalm and Perdomo to all [MATH], thereby replacing the constant [MATH] in their result by [MATH].
tldr: The paper determines the critical value for the Beurling-type theorem in weighted Bergman spaces by constructing invariant subspaces that fail the wandering subspace property.
motivation: The work aims to characterize when zero-based invariant subspaces in weighted Bergman spaces possess the wandering subspace property, confirming a conjecture of Shimorin.
method: The authors construct finite sets for each parameter and extend the prescribed-curvature construction of Hedenmalm and Perdomo to a broader range of weights.
result: They show that the Beurling-type theorem holds on the weighted Bergman space if and only if the parameter is below a critical value, replacing a constant in earlier results.
conclusion: This resolves Shimorin's conjecture and generalizes the prescribed-curvature construction to all relevant parameters.

title: Singed: Correct Outputs Do Not Certify Safe Execution In Llm Agents
authors: Xiaoyu Xu, Zi Liang, Minxin Du, Qipeng Xie, Qingqing Ye, Yuyuan Li, Haibo Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents select and execute third-party artifacts. Different implementations can return the requested output while producing hidden execution effects that task-, attack-, or choice-based evaluations may miss. We study functional counterfeits: implementations that match benign alternatives on the requested output but add an effect forbidden by the task contract. We introduce SINGED (Source Integrity and the Nonidentifiability Gap in Execution Decisions for LLM Agents), a controlled benchmark covering five primary and two held-out task families. It varies displayed rank, evidence depth, decision policy, model release, and agent configuration, while task and process oracles verify the artifact and execution path. Across 7,549 audited trials, the randomized-rank study finds counterfeit execution in 45% (27/60) of rank-one trials and none at later ranks. Cross-candidate comparison eliminates shallow failures and reduces layered failures from 15.7% to 4.2%, but leaves dependency failures; its benefit is uncertain on unseen effects and public-package structures. Moreover, seven releases with no counterfeit executions when benign alternatives are available execute the counterfeit in 55/175 single-source cells after alternatives are removed. SINGED thus exposes a rank-, evidence-, and choice-sensitive outcome-to-execution gap: evaluation must connect correct outputs to execution paths.
tldr: The paper introduces SINGED, a benchmark showing that correct task outputs from LLM agents do not guarantee safe execution paths, due to functional counterfeits that match requested outputs while adding forbidden effects.
motivation: Tool-using LLM agents can select third-party implementations that appear correct but hide unsafe execution effects, which existing task-, attack-, or choice-based evaluations may overlook.
method: The authors build a controlled benchmark across five primary and two held-out task families, varying displayed rank, evidence depth, decision policy, model release, and agent configuration, while task and process oracles verify artifacts and execution paths.
result: Across 7,549 audited trials, counterfeit execution occurred in 45% of rank-one trials but none at later ranks; cross-candidate comparison reduced layered failures from 15.7% to 4.2% but left dependency failures, and removing benign alternatives led to counterfeit execution in 55/175 single-source cells.
conclusion: Evaluation of LLM agents must connect correct outputs to execution paths, as output correctness alone is insufficient to certify safe execution.

title: Privacy-Friendly Cohort Determination: Sealed, CSP-Independent In-Browser Ml Inference Of Professional Segments For Identity-Less Advertising
authors: Om Shankar Tiwari, Navnit Shukla, Guanyu Wang, Akshay Jain
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: B2B advertising targets a viewer's professional attributes (employer size and industry, function, seniority) and has obtained them by matching identities across sites. Safari and Firefox block third-party cookies, Google retired the Privacy Sandbox cohort APIs in 2025, and reverse-IP firmographics decay under remote work. We present SIF (Sealed Inference Frame), which infers coarse professional cohorts on the device and emits only a locally differentially private, taxonomy-coded label into the OpenRTB bid stream, with no cross-site identifier. It rests on a property of the web platform we make precise: a navigated cross-origin iframe is the only way third-party code obtains a policy it controls, so inference runs in WebAssembly even where the publisher's CSP forbids it, and a nested worker served with default-src 'none' gives the model no network. Even a malicious model leaks at most about 5 bits per site per week. Labels pass through a memoised k-ary randomised response keyed to the publisher's first-party identifier, which gives [MATH]-local differential privacy, defeats averaging, and links requests no better than the identifier already sent. An org-conditional k-anonymity rule suppresses cells, more strictly on corporate networks than at home. Cohorts ride OpenRTB user.data in a LinkedIn-aligned taxonomy, and attribution uses LinkedIn's click-scoped li_fat_id without bridging identities. We report a crawl of CSP deployment on 7,969 top sites and 431 B2B publishers, Heavy-Ad budgets, closed-form privacy-utility trade-offs, a re-identification simulation, and an assessment of which attributes are predictable at all: company type and size are, seniority largely is not. On-device is a design property, not a consent exemption.
tldr: SIF is an in-browser WebAssembly inference system for privacy-preserving professional cohort targeting in identity-less advertising, using local differential privacy and CSP-independent iframe execution.
motivation: Third-party cookie blocking, retirement of Privacy Sandbox cohort APIs, and decaying reverse-IP firmographics motivate an on-device method to infer coarse B2B professional attributes without cross-site identifiers.
method: A sealed cross-origin iframe runs WebAssembly inference under a nested worker with default-src 'none', emits a locally differentially private taxonomy-coded label via memoised k-ary randomised response, and applies org-conditional k-anonymity suppression before OpenRTB user.data output.
result: The authors report a crawl of CSP deployment across 7,969 top sites and 431 B2B publishers, heavy-ad budget analysis, closed-form privacy-utility trade-offs, a re-identification simulation, and attribute predictability showing company type and size are predictable while seniority largely is not.
conclusion: On-device inference is presented as a design property rather than a consent exemption, enabling privacy-friendly coarse professional cohort signaling in the OpenRTB bid stream without cross-site identity bridging.

title: Proofs Without Nominals: G\"odel's Ontological Argument, Its Shallow Embedding, And The Open Questions Of The Monatshefte Notes
authors: Christoph Benzm\"uller
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzm\"uller and Scott's Notes on G\"odel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument (2025), reaches beyond the modal object language of the arguments: its property quantifiers range over terms that may also express nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic, and a proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding that need not be one of the modal logic. That the framework affords this is not new, and whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled in two ways: by replaying it in an explicit proof calculus, done by hand for chosen theorems, or by analysing the proofs the embedding itself produces, which this article does mechanically, for every result at once. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof inside the object language: 294 written out by hand and machine-checked, none using a nominal. The proofs the Notes themselves give instantiate no nominal either; what the detector flags there are terms a prover substituted. The three questions the Notes leave open are settled too, and without nominals, but the conjunction axiom has to be emended: generalised in the Notes to G\"odel's "any number of summands", it covers the conjunction of no properties, and of one; the empty one alone settles all three, and the two together yield what a separate axiom of G\"odel's is for. This article restricts the conjunction axiom to at least two different conjuncts, the reading G\"odel's footnote suggests, and the questions are settled again, by proofs that turn on the argument rather than a degenerate instance. The restriction holds of the object language only: with a nominal the axioms make the accessibility relation the identity and the readings coincide. Every theorem is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4; the countermodels are Nitpick's, certified by the build.
tldr: The paper mechanically analyzes shallow embeddings of Gödel's ontological argument, settling open questions without hybrid-logic nominals and restricting the conjunction axiom.
motivation: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic may allow proofs involving nominals that are not theorems of the modal object language, raising questions about the legitimacy of the formalized results.
method: The author uses a mechanical proof detector to analyze all statements from the Notes, replays key proofs by hand, and verifies results in Isabelle/HOL and Lean 4 with Nitpick countermodels.
result: All 294 hand-proved statements are shown to be provable without nominals; the three open questions are settled with a restricted conjunction axiom, and the restriction is shown to hold only of the object language.
conclusion: The embedding framework is refined to avoid degenerate conjunctions and confirm that the Notes' results lie within the modal object language, though the work is entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Calibrating One-Round Membership Inference With Neighbors
authors: Francesco Rita, Jie Zhang, Florian Tram\`er
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The state-of-the-art Membership Inference (MI) methods calibrate their signal separately for each example using reference models, auxiliary models trained to exclude the target. This paradigm scales poorly to modern large models, however, whose training is too expensive to replicate. This has motivated one-round settings, where only a single trained model is available; but without reference models the per-example calibration that drives the strongest attacks can no longer be estimated, leaving the membership signal weak. We ask whether neighbors of the target point can recover this calibration without training any additional model. Our key observation is that reference models serve only to reveal how an example behaves under models not trained on it, and that querying the target model on nearby samples yields the same information. We propose two complementary ways to obtain such neighbors, and show that querying them against an early training checkpoint further sharpens the signal. We evaluate across three image classification datasets and three training setups, showing that neighbors yield strong membership signals and competitive attack performance at no additional training cost.
tldr: The paper proposes using neighboring samples, queried on an early training checkpoint, to calibrate one-round membership inference attacks without reference models.
motivation: State-of-the-art membership inference relies on reference models for per-example calibration, which is impractical for modern large models whose training cannot be replicated, motivating one-round settings where only a single trained model is available.
method: The authors observe that reference models merely reveal how an example behaves under models not trained on it, and show that querying the target model on nearby samples provides the same information; they propose two ways to obtain neighbors and sharpen the signal using an early training checkpoint.
result: Experiments across three image classification datasets and three training setups show that neighbors yield strong membership signals and competitive attack performance at no additional training cost.
conclusion: Neighbors can effectively recover calibration for one-round membership inference, offering a scalable alternative to reference-model-based approaches.

title: Sample Complexity Of Equivariant Reinforcement Learning
authors: Rayan Mazouz, Haibo Zhao, Chris Hillar, Christian Shewmake
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful framework for robotic control, yet its practical application is often hindered by high sample complexity. This is particularly restrictive in physical domains where interaction data is costly. While the world often exhibits geometric and physical symmetries, standard RL algorithms typically fail to exploit this structure. In this paper, we demonstrate that exploiting group symmetries significantly reduces the sample complexity of RL. Focusing on finite-horizon Markov decision processes, we find that leveraging homomorphisms induced by group symmetries significantly reduces the theoretical upper and lower bounds on the number of environment interactions required to reach an optimal return. We further extend these bounds to continuous state and action spaces, providing corresponding sample-complexity guarantees under appropriate regularity assumptions. Beyond theory, we validate our findings through controlled experiments and demonstrate the advantages of symmetry-aware policy learning on high-dimensional continuous robotic simulations. Our results show that integrating symmetry into the learning pipeline yields substantial gains in sample efficiency and performance, offering a principled path toward more data-efficient robotics.
tldr: The paper shows that exploiting group symmetries reduces sample complexity in finite-horizon reinforcement learning, with theoretical bounds and robotic simulation experiments.
motivation: Standard reinforcement learning suffers from high sample complexity, especially in physical robotics where interaction data is costly; geometric and physical symmetries are often ignored by standard algorithms.
method: The authors analyze finite-horizon Markov decision processes with group symmetries, deriving improved upper and lower sample-complexity bounds via induced homomorphisms, and extend the results to continuous state-action spaces under regularity assumptions.
result: Symmetry-aware policy learning yields substantial gains in sample efficiency and performance on high-dimensional continuous robotic simulations, supported by theoretical upper and lower bounds.
conclusion: Integrating group symmetry into the learning pipeline offers a principled path toward more data-efficient robotics, though the work is classical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Polynomial Time Characterization For Strongly Efx Orientable Graphs
authors: Jinghan A Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete fair division is the problem of dividing a discrete set of goods among agents in a fair manner. In this setting, one of the most sought-after notions of fairness is envy-freeness up to any good (EFX). In 2023, Christodoulou, Fiat, Koutsoupias, and Sgouritsa introduced the idea of a graphical valuation, where the fair division problem is represented by a simple graph where vertices are the agents and the edges are the goods, and each vertex only values incident edges. They showed that an EFX allocation always exists, while determining the existence of an EFX orientation is NP-hard. They posed an open question of determining which graphs always admitted an EFX orientation regardless of valuation. These graphs, called strongly EFX orientable graphs, were first studied by Zeng and Mehta in 2025, who demonstrated that all such graphs have chromatic number at most 3, and bipartite graphs always admit an EFX orientation regardless of valuation. In this manuscript, we finish resolving this question by giving a polynomial time characterization of strongly EFX orientable graphs. In particular, we show that a connected graph [MATH] is strongly EFX orientable if and only if either of the following is true: (1) [MATH] is bipartite, or (2) the block decomposition of [MATH] contains exactly one nonbipartite block [MATH], and there exists a vertex [MATH] such that the degree of [MATH] within [MATH] is 2 and [MATH] is bipartite. This proof was discovered by AI, with human intervention to break the problem into the appropriate subproblems.
tldr: This paper gives a polynomial-time characterization of strongly EFX orientable graphs, fully resolving an open problem in discrete fair division of goods on graphs.
motivation: Fair division of indivisible goods under envy-freeness up to any good (EFX) is a central problem, and the graphical valuation model introduced by Christodoulou et al. left open which graphs always admit an EFX orientation regardless of valuation.
method: The authors build on prior work (Zeng and Mehta 2025) showing strong EFX orientability implies chromatic number at most 3, using block decomposition of graphs and structural analysis of nonbipartite blocks to derive a polynomial-time decision criterion.
result: A connected graph is strongly EFX orientable if and only if it is bipartite, or its block decomposition has exactly one nonbipartite block with a vertex of degree 2 within the block such that removing it leaves a bipartite graph.
conclusion: The open question of characterizing strongly EFX orientable graphs is completely resolved via a polynomial-time characterization, with the proof partly discovered by AI.

title: Local Predictability And Collective Fidelity In LLM-Agent Societies
authors: Igor Itkin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact surrogates could reduce the cost of simulating large language model societies, but must reproduce collective behavior. We compare individual predictions and collective forecasts using 9,455 published trajectories and new experiments on opinion dynamics. Neighbor information improves individual prediction in all 16 public-data settings and pooled collective forecasts on held-out questions, although collective gains depend on transfer conditions. Tests on 24 new statements do not confirm earlier contrasting history effects in forecasts from the initial state. Qwen benefits from history after three observed rounds. These findings motivate direct collective validation, explicit limits on available observations, and comparisons with simple baselines.
tldr: The paper evaluates compact surrogate models for predicting collective opinion dynamics in large language model agent societies, comparing individual predictions against pooled collective forecasts.
motivation: Simulating large LLM-agent societies is expensive, so cheaper surrogate models are desirable, but only if they faithfully reproduce emergent collective behavior rather than just individual responses.
method: Using 9,455 published trajectories plus new experiments on opinion dynamics, the study systematically compares individual-level predictions and collective forecasts with and without neighbor information, across 16 public-data settings and 24 newly designed statements.
result: Neighbor information improves individual prediction in all 16 settings and pooled collective forecasts on held-out questions, though collective gains depend on transfer conditions; earlier contrasting history effects were not confirmed on the new statements, while Qwen benefited from history after three observed rounds.
conclusion: The authors advocate direct collective validation of surrogates, explicit limits on available observations, and comparison against simple baselines when modeling LLM-agent societies.

title: Travel Mode- And Purpose-Specific Origin-Destination Matrices For England And Wales From Fused Travel Survey And Mobile Network Data
authors: Bowen Zhang, Chen Zhong, Mingfei Ma, James Golding-Graham
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Origin-destination (OD) matrices sit behind much of quantitative transport planning, from model calibration and accessibility analysis to the appraisal of new services and development. The increasing emphasis on place-based solutions requires mobility data that can support decision-making not only at the strategic level, but also at finer spatial scales. This requires up-to-date OD evidence at small-area resolution, disaggregated by travel mode and purpose, which remains either inaccessible or unavailable. In this work, we present dense MSOA-to-MSOA OD matrices for England and Wales, segmented by seven travel modes and representative time periods, with eight trip purposes for the weekday morning peak. The matrices are built by calibrating aggregate mobile network data provided by BT against National Travel Survey (NTS), census and trip-rate evidence, preserving the observed spatial structure of movement while referencing its age, mode and purpose composition to the survey. The open-source data processing pipeline is released alongside the matrices, so that the construction of the dataset can be inspected in full and adapted to other years, regions or assumptions.
tldr: The paper constructs travel mode- and purpose-specific MSOA-level origin-destination matrices for England and Wales by fusing mobile network data with national travel survey data.
motivation: Transport planning increasingly demands fine-grained, up-to-date mobility data disaggregated by travel mode and trip purpose, which is largely unavailable at small-area resolution.
method: Aggregate mobile network data from BT is calibrated against National Travel Survey, census and trip-rate evidence to preserve observed spatial movement structure while inferring age, mode and purpose composition, with an open-source processing pipeline released.
result: Dense MSOA-to-MSOA OD matrices covering seven travel modes, multiple time periods, and eight trip purposes for the weekday morning peak are produced for England and Wales.
conclusion: The dataset and pipeline provide transferable small-area mobility evidence applicable to other years, regions or assumptions, supporting place-based transport decision-making.

title: A Branch-Free General Renormalization Scheme For Pair Arithmetic And Its Performance Evaluation
authors: Tomonori Kouya
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pair arithmetic omits the renormalization stage performed at the end of each operation of multi-component multiple-precision arithmetic, reducing the operation count and, by eliminating conditional branches, easing SIMD vectorization. Renormalization cannot be omitted entirely, however, because iterative solvers may then fail to converge. We propose RenormBF-pair, a branch-free fixed-trip-count renormalizer parameterized by the word count \(K\) and the input length \(n\): a VecSum sweep, a tail fold, and \(r\) rounds of a FastTwoSum chain, costing \(6(n-1)+(n-K)+3r(K-1)\) flops. Over \(200{,}000\) trials per condition, the smallest round count producing no non-overlap violation was \(r=1\) for \(K \leq 3\) and \(r=2\) for \(K=4\), whereas the same cost spent on a VecSum\(K\)-style TwoSum chain fails for \(K=4\). We delimit with explicit counterexamples both the input condition under which the sum relation holds and the fact that the scheme does not, in general, guarantee a correctly rounded lowest component. Integrating it into CG and BiCGStab over pair arithmetic in binary64 and binary32, we sweep \(240\) paired runs including real matrices screened from SuiteSparse. The proposed scheme and VecSum\(K\) returned bitwise identical words wherever both succeeded, so they are indistinguishable for CG in binary64; differences appear only where VecSum\(K\) breaks, namely binary32 and BiCGStab. There the \(22\)--\(16\) win--loss record is not significant (sign test, \(p=0.42\)); the clear bias is structural, non-overlap violations dropping from \(66\) rows to \(37\). The cost is \(+3.4\%\) for the whole CG solver.
tldr: The paper proposes RenormBF-pair, a branch-free fixed-trip-count renormalization scheme for pair arithmetic, and evaluates its performance in iterative solvers like CG and BiCGStab.
motivation: Pair arithmetic omits per-operation renormalization to reduce operation count and enable SIMD vectorization, but complete omission can cause iterative solvers to fail to converge.
method: The scheme uses a VecSum sweep, a tail fold, and r rounds of a FastTwoSum chain, with a flop cost of 6(n-1)+(n-K)+3r(K-1); it is tested over 200,000 trials per condition and integrated into CG and BiCGStab on binary64 and binary32 matrices.
result: The smallest round count producing no non-overlap violation was r=1 for K<=3 and r=2 for K=4; the scheme matched VecSumK bitwise where both succeeded, with non-overlap violations dropping from 66 to 37 rows at a +3.4% CG cost.
conclusion: The authors delimit conditions for the sum relation and show the scheme does not generally guarantee a correctly rounded lowest component, making it a practical but limited renormalization technique.

title: Student Perceptions Of Tablet-Based Teaching And Learning In Tne Undergraduate Mathematics
authors: Dimitrios Chiotis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tablet-based teaching and learning has become increasingly common in university mathematics courses, offering capabilities such as digital ink, dynamic visualisation, and real-time annotation. However, there is limited experiential evidence regarding how students perceive the specific benefits and drawbacks of tablet-supported teaching and learning, particularly in Transnational Education (TNE) settings. This paper presents results from a small-scale exploratory survey of undergraduate students ([MATH]) attending mathematics courses within an applied sciences degree programme, who anonymously rated a set of statements regarding their experiences with tablet-based instruction on a five-point Likert scale. Initial analysis shows that students in this cohort perceived tablet teaching most positively in supporting step-by-step understanding and active engagement during lectures through real-time annotation and structured note-taking. In contrast, perceptions related to long-term recall, interest in mathematics, and preference over alternative teaching methods were more mixed. These findings suggest that students in this cohort perceived tablet-based teaching positively for supporting procedural understanding, while perceptions of other aspects of learning appeared more varied.
tldr: A small-scale survey study reporting undergraduate mathematics students' perceptions of tablet-based teaching and learning in a transnational education setting.
motivation: Tablet-based instruction is increasingly used in university mathematics, yet experiential evidence on how students perceive its benefits and drawbacks—especially in Transnational Education (TNE) contexts—remains limited.
method: An anonymous exploratory survey was administered to undergraduate applied-science students using a five-point Likert scale to rate statements about their experiences with tablet-based instruction, followed by initial descriptive analysis.
result: Students perceived tablets most positively for supporting step-by-step understanding and active lecture engagement via real-time annotation and structured note-taking, while perceptions of long-term recall, interest in mathematics, and preference over other methods were mixed.
conclusion: Tablet-based teaching appears to support procedural understanding in this cohort, but its perceived value for broader learning outcomes is more variable, motivating further and larger-scale investigation.

title: A Projected Descent Method For Minimization Of Weakly Semismooth Functions Over Polyhedral Sets
authors: Majid Soleimani-Damaneh Morteza Maleknia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a projection-based descent method for minimizing weakly semismooth functions over polyhedral sets, taking an initial step toward extending projection-based descent algorithms to nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems. At each iteration, the method considers an inner approximation of the Clarke [MATH]-subdifferential at the current iterate over the feasible region and uses its least-norm element to generate a search direction. An exponential limited backtracking line search is then developed to assess the quality of the generated direction, while a projected variant of Mifflin's line search is proposed to identify nonredundant subgradients that enrich the Clarke [MATH]-subdifferential approximation when necessary. To quantify stationarity, a characterization of stationary points based on the projection operator yields a computable optimality measure for the proposed method. The convergence properties of the proposed method are established under mild assumptions. If the algorithm generates infinitely many serious steps, we identify two subsequences such that every cluster point of each subsequence is stationary. If the number of serious steps is finite, we show that the final serious step generates a stationary point. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficiency and broad applicability of the proposed method across a wide range of test problems, including applications in image denoising, multiobjective optimization, and data clustering. To extend the applicability of the proposed method to problems with general smooth nonlinear constraints, we propose a heuristic approach based on sequential linearization.
tldr: The paper develops a projection-based descent method for minimizing weakly semismooth functions over polyhedral sets, extending projection algorithms to nonsmooth nonconvex optimization.
motivation: Nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization over polyhedral feasible sets is challenging, and existing projection-based descent methods have not been extended to weakly semismooth functions, motivating a new algorithmic framework.
method: At each iteration the method uses the least-norm element of an inner approximation of the Clarke subdifferential to generate a search direction, combined with an exponential limited backtracking line search and a projected variant of Mifflin's line search to identify nonredundant subgradients.
result: Convergence is established under mild assumptions: cluster points of subsequences of serious steps are stationary, and a finite number of serious steps yields a stationary final point; numerical experiments span image denoising, multiobjective optimization, and data clustering.
conclusion: The proposed method offers an efficient, broadly applicable approach to nonsmooth nonconvex optimization over polyhedral sets, with a heuristic sequential-linearization extension for general smooth nonlinear constraints.

title: SaplingGuard: A Multidimensional-Profile-Aware Multi-Agent Guardrail For Developmentally Safe Adolescent-LLM Interaction
authors: Jing Tan, Yifan Liu, Yi Lin, Xinwei Guo, Ziwei Wang, Xiangyu Zhao, Lei Ma, Xin Yao, Xuetao Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As adolescents increasingly use LLMs in everyday life, ensuring safe and developmentally appropriate responses has become essential. However, existing LLM guardrails primarily target explicit harmful content in isolated prompts or responses and are less effective at identifying implicit, context-dependent developmental risks. To address this limitation, we propose SaplingGuard, a plug-and-play, profile-aware and dialogue-aware guardrail that requires no modification to downstream model parameters. SaplingGuard decomposes adolescent safety intervention into three specialized agents for user profile construction, context-aware risk assessment, and intent-preserving prompt optimization. Together, these agents leverage the current prompt, preceding dialogue, and structured user characteristics to identify contextual risks and guide downstream response generation. We evaluate SaplingGuard on SaplingBench, which contains 276 three-turn dialogues spanning seven categories of developmental risk. Across ten adolescent profile conditions and nine open- and closed-source downstream LLMs, profile-aware retrieval improves the Major Hit rate from 50.8% to 63.7+/-1.1%. End-to-end intervention further reduces the average harmful response rate from 17.10% to 5.27% and increases the average safety score from 0.7017 to 1.0043. These results show that user-profile and dialogue context provide complementary signals for identifying implicit developmental risks, and that SaplingGuard can serve as an effective external safety layer for adolescent-LLM interaction.
tldr: SaplingGuard is a plug-and-play, profile- and dialogue-aware multi-agent guardrail that makes LLM interactions developmentally safer for adolescents.
motivation: Existing LLM guardrails mostly target explicit harmful content in isolated prompts and fail to catch implicit, context-dependent developmental risks that arise in ongoing adolescent conversations.
method: The framework decomposes adolescent safety intervention into three specialized agents: user-profile construction, context-aware risk assessment, and intent-preserving prompt optimization, requiring no changes to downstream model parameters and leveraging the current prompt, prior dialogue, and structured user characteristics.
result: Evaluated on SaplingBench (276 three-turn dialogues, seven risk categories, ten profile conditions, nine LLMs), profile-aware retrieval raised the Major Hit rate from 50.8% to 63.7±1.1%, while end-to-end intervention cut the harmful response rate from 17.10% to 5.27% and improved the safety score from 0.7017 to 1.0043.
conclusion: User profiles and dialogue context provide complementary signals for detecting implicit developmental risks, and SaplingGuard can act as an effective external safety layer for adolescent-LLM interaction.

title: Cheap To Hypothesize, Costly To Verify: The Defense Surface Of Agentic Vulnerability Discovery
authors: Kaikai Zhang, Zihan Zhang, Yuchong Xie, Zesen Liu, Shuangjie Yao, Zhixiang Zhang, Dongdong She
abstract: ArXiv:2609.35909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents turn vulnerability discovery into a repository-scale search: they generate many vulnerability hypotheses but can verify only a subset under a finite budget. We show that autonomous vulnerability discovery exhibits a hypothesis-verification asymmetry, where verifying a candidate hypothesis through reachability analysis, execution, and proof-of-concept construction is substantially more expensive than forming it. Under a finite resource budget, this makes autonomous discovery a resource-bounded selective-verification process, further exposing verification effort as a unique defense surface. We present RedHerring, which inserts certifiably safe decoys that divert verification effort from real vulnerabilities. Each decoy combines a CVE-derived vulnerability chain that attracts verification with a false bridge that keeps its dangerous sink unreachable. A private certificate lets the defender verify this property efficiently, while establishing the same fact from the released repository requires solving a computationally hard problem. RedHerring further adapts each decoy to the target repository so that it reads as ordinary program logic. Across 33 OSS-Fuzz projects, 70 evaluation instances, and five models under matched budgets, RedHerring reduces real vulnerabilities discovered by 38.7-60.4%. Trajectory analysis shows that agents spend 30.6-51.5% of completion tokens and an estimated 32.5-49.9% of runtime verifying decoys, showing that RedHerring redirects a substantial fraction of the fixed search budget toward decoys. When explicitly informed that decoys may be present, the agent adapts its search strategy, yet RedHerring still reduces vulnerabilities discovered by 37.2% relative to an informed Baseline, showing that its effectiveness does not depend on decoy secrecy.
tldr: The paper introduces RedHerring, a defense that inserts certifiably safe decoy vulnerabilities into repositories to divert LLM agents' limited verification budget away from real vulnerabilities.
motivation: Autonomous LLM agents can generate many vulnerability hypotheses but can only verify a subset under finite budgets, creating a hypothesis-verification asymmetry that can be exploited for defense.
method: RedHerring constructs decoys combining a CVE-derived vulnerability chain to attract verification with a false bridge making the dangerous sink unreachable, and uses a private certificate to let defenders efficiently verify safety while making independent verification computationally hard.
result: Across 33 OSS-Fuzz projects, 70 evaluation instances, and five models under matched budgets, RedHerring reduced real vulnerabilities discovered by 38.7–60.4%, with agents spending 30.6–51.5% of completion tokens and an estimated 32.5–49.9% of runtime on decoys; it still reduced discoveries by 37.2% against an informed baseline.
conclusion: The effectiveness of RedHerring does not depend on decoy secrecy and establishes verification effort as a novel defense surface in autonomous vulnerability discovery.

title: TTMark: Pairwise Distortion-Free Watermarking Beyond Single-Token Entropy
authors: Ruibo Chen, Zhengmian Hu, Donghang Lu, Xuehao Cui, Georgios Milis, Yihan Wu, Jian Du, Heng Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distortion-free watermarking enables reliable attribution of machine-generated text while preserving output distribution. However, existing methods operate independently on each generated token, making their detection capability fundamentally constrained by the entropy of the next-token distribution. We present Tandem Token WaterMark (TTMARK), a general pairwise watermarking framework that extends distortion-free watermarking from individual tokens to adjacent token pairs. By watermarking the joint distribution of consecutive tokens, TTMARK enlarges the effective watermarking alphabet from V to [MATH], allowing the detector to exploit both token entropy and conditional entropy while preserving distortion-freeness over the joint distribution. We further introduce a branch-isolating concatenated tandem generation algorithm that efficiently constructs the joint distribution in a single forward pass. Theoretically, we show that pairwise watermarking achieves better expected detection strength in low-entropy regimes. Extensive experiments across multiple language models, datasets, and three representative distortion-free watermarking schemes demonstrate that TTMARK consistently improves detectability without degrading generation quality, while also improving robustness to edits and substantially enhancing localized watermark detection.
tldr: TTMARK is a pairwise, distortion-free watermarking framework for machine-generated text that watermarks joint distributions of adjacent token pairs to boost detection strength.
motivation: Existing distortion-free watermarking schemes operate token-by-token, so detection power is fundamentally limited by the next-token entropy and degrades in low-entropy regimes.
method: The authors extend distortion-free watermarking from single tokens to adjacent token pairs (enlarging the effective alphabet from V to V^2), and introduce a branch-isolating concatenated tandem generation algorithm that builds the joint distribution in a single forward pass.
result: Theory shows better expected detection strength in low-entropy regimes, and experiments across multiple LLMs, datasets, and three distortion-free schemes show improved detectability, robustness to edits, and localized detection without quality loss.
conclusion: Pairwise watermarking generalizes and improves distortion-free text watermarking, offering stronger and more robust attribution of LLM-generated text.

title: Know The Normal, Track The Attack: Context-Grounded And Stateful Llm Investigation Over System Provenance
authors: Lijie Zheng, Ji He, Ying Wang, Huang Zhang, Yulong Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.36494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Provenance-based intrusion detection systems (PIDSs) identify suspicious activity in audit streams, but their outputs remain difficult to turn into coherent attack narratives. Direct LLM analyses of local anomalous subgraphs lack deployment-specific normal-behavior knowledge and validated attack state across evidence fragments. This can cause unsupported attack interpretations of routine activities and incorrect attribution of temporally dispersed evidence to attack stages. We present ANCHOR, an investigation-oriented provenance system that combines evidence curation with context-grounded LLM reasoning. It calibrates anomaly judgments by relation type and links anomalous windows through rare relation-role patterns. The resulting evidence queues preserve causal structure, temporal boundaries, and cross-window continuity. The investigator interprets process-centered evidence using two complementary forms of context. Deployment Context combines environment-specific interaction and object baselines with high-risk security knowledge. Case Context uses a confidence-gated Attack-Tracking Cache to maintain investigation state across windows. Correlating current evidence with high-confidence prior findings, ANCHOR incrementally reconstructs attack narratives organized by kill-chain stages. We evaluate ANCHOR on six DARPA Transparent Computing E3/E5 datasets across three operating systems. Controlled evidence-level and end-to-end comparisons show improved overall IoC recovery and attack-stage attribution over state-of-the-art provenance-based baselines.
